title: An Ontology-Driven MCP Agent Framework for Ensuring Integrity in Architectural Structural Design
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Model (LLM)-based autonomous agents has demonstrated strong potential for automating knowledge-intensive tasks. However, their probabilistic reasoning often leads to hallucinations and weak domain knowledge integrity, limiting their applicability in high-stakes architecture, engineering, and construction (Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC)) contexts where engineering reliability is critical. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel architecture, termed the Ontology-driven Model Context Protocol (O-MCP) Framework, which integrates formal ontology with the standardized Model Context Protocol to ensure logical consistency and trustworthy knowledge exchange. The framework introduces a three-layer architecture consisting of a Knowledge and Data Source Layer, a Semantic MCP Server Layer, and an Intelligent Agent Layer. Its core contribution is the Semantic MCP Server, which incorporates a semantic guardrail mechanism that validates agent requests in real time using ontology-based reasoning. A case study in architectural structural design illustrates how the framework formalizes expert tacit knowledge and preserves decentralized knowledge sovereignty. A proof-of-concept experiment in reinforced concrete slab design positions O-MCP as a reference standard for formalized expert knowledge. Results show that while LLM-based RAG systems achieve approximately 83% agreement, systematic errors persist in numerical reasoning and multi-condition rule application, highlighting the value of formal ontological verification for guaranteeing engineering integrity.

title: AgentEsc: A Taxonomy of Privilege-Escalation Threats in Tool-Calling and MCP-Based Agent Systems
abstract: AgentEsc is an open taxonomy and benchmark for privilege-escalation threats in agentic AI systems that use tool-calling, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), or multi-agent orchestration. It provides a five-class taxonomy with fifteen testable sub-techniques, a declarative scenario schema, and metrics (Escalation Success Rate, Detection Rate, Containment Rate) evaluated across a defense ladder, enabling reproducible measurement of authorization-boundary vulnerabilities in agent frameworks.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Blockchain Reputation Oracles: An MCP-Based Study
abstract: Trust evaluation remains a key challenge in decentralized systems, where conventional reputation mechanisms often reduce complex human feedback to simple scores. This study employs the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—a standardized coordination framework—to connect Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning with blockchain-based verification. Under MCP supervision, contextual retrieval, semantic inference, and on-chain validation are organized into a reproducible workflow that converts unstructured textual data into verifiable trust metrics.
venue: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Emerging Trends in Software Engineering for Blockchain (WETSEB)

It grounds agents in STAC metadata and confines them to validated cloud-native engines — SQL over Parquet on S3 via DuckDB with H3 spatial indexing — so they can query terabyte-scale data without downloading it, misreading it, or silently failing at scale. Runs locally for sensitive data or on autoscaling Kubernetes for scale.

title: Pipeline Inspection, Visualization, and Interoperability in PyTerrier
abstract: PyTerrier provides a declarative framework for building and experimenting with Information Retrieval (IR) pipelines. In this demonstration, we highlight several recent pipeline operations that improve their ability to be programmatically inspected, visualized, and integrated with other tools (via the Model Context Protocol, MCP). These capabilities aim to make it easier for researchers, students, and AI agents to understand and use a wide array of IR pipelines.

title: Folklore Clinical Variant Interpretation MCP
abstract: The official public, read-only Model Context Protocol adapter for Folklore by Helena Bioinformatics. It gives AI clients structured access to public germline variant evidence, automated ACMG/AMP decision support, provenance, and related literature. The adapter accepts no patient, phenotype, family, or case context. Folklore's proprietary interpretation backend and evidence database are not included.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: AgriGuard AI: A Cloud-Agnostic Multi-Agent System for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Agriculture remains one of the most operationally complex and environmentally sensitive industries in the modern world. This paper presents AgriGuard AI, a cloud-agnostic multi-agent agricultural intelligence system integrating Retrieval- Augmented Generation (RAG), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Kubernetes-orchestrated infrastructure, and risk-aware reason- ing pipelines for scalable precision agriculture. The proposed framework integrates heterogeneous agricultural data sources including environmental telemetry, soil-health databases, crop pathology repositories, and government policy systems to provide contextual agricultural advisory services. The architecture sup- ports distributed multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-grounded reasoning, AI safety guardrails, multilingual interaction, and cloud-native deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and edge- computing environments. IX. MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL INTEGRATIONmodels for risk estimation, yield prediction, nutrient depletion, and retrieval optimization are introduced. Experimental and scalability considerations are also discussed to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system for real- world agricultural intelligence applications.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: cdc-health-mcp-server
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the CDC Open Data portal (~1,487 public health datasets via the Socrata SODA API), providing dataset catalog discovery, schema inspection, and SoQL queries across disease surveillance, mortality, vaccinations, behavioral risk factors, and other public health domains.

abstract: Defensive publication establishing prior art for a unified Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway architecture. Discloses self-referential implementation-agent dispatch, webhook-driven self-deployment with content-aware strategy selection, and autonomous event-driven processing pipelines embedded within an MCP gateway. Validated by adversarial prior art survey of 22 open-source projects, 10 commercial products, 6 academic publications, and 2 US patent filings.

title: The Super-Gems Framework v3.0: Custom Video Game Studio Lattice Phonebook
abstract: This paper presents the Super-Gems Framework v3.0, a Byzantine-fault-tolerant structural lattice designed to orchestrate 20 specialized agent-nodes for independent video game development under the NinjaLady44 operational banner. The framework addresses epistemic uncertainty through an affine multi-objective affinity routing function, utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool hooks to manage production requests and maintain system state integrity.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: canli-validation-mcp: an MCP server that validates backtests
abstract: A Model Context Protocol server that validates a trading backtest for an AI coding assistant: deflated Sharpe ratio, CSCV probability of backtest overfitting, minimum track record and backtest length, haircut Sharpe ratio and luck-equivalent trials, each checked against its source paper, with Ed25519-signed receipts and a statement of what each result does not establish.

title: mysql-ops-mcp: a read-only-first MCP server for agent access to SSH-only MySQL databases
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets an AI agent query a private MySQL database safely. It maintains its own SSH tunnel so the database never needs a public port, validates every statement against a read-only whitelist before execution, and keeps state-changing tools (restart / deploy) unregistered unless they are explicitly enabled.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: zotero-native-mcp: an MCP server for Zotero 10+ over its native local API
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that reads and writes a Zotero 10+ library entirely offline through Zotero's native local API, with no Zotero plugin, no zotero.org API key and no cloud round trip. It lets AI assistants search a library, read PDF full text, create collections, add references and attach local PDFs.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: openfec-mcp-server
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the OpenFEC REST API, providing U.S. federal campaign finance data — candidates, political committees, itemized and aggregated contributions (Schedule A), disbursements (Schedule B), independent expenditures (Schedule E), filings, elections, calendar, and FEC legal documents (advisory opinions, enforcement cases).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Beyond Detection: Autonomous Anomaly Remediation for MCP Against Tool Poisoning Attacks
abstract: LLM-powered agents are evolving from passive recommenders into autonomous executors, leveraging tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for web automation. However, this paradigm introduces a new vulnerability: tool poisoning attacks that manipulate the MCP context can corrupt an agent's reasoning. Existing methods focus on anomaly detection and lack autonomous correction mechanisms, hindering their real-world deployment.

title: Data Galactica MCP server
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for resolve any person or company to one permanent ID (KYB, CIN/LEI/SEC CIK/Wikidata resolution), usable from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients. Website: https://datagalactica.comSource: https://github.com/rchtjn2-gif/datagalactica-mcp-server
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: AGENTIC AI AUTOMATION OF UNICOS APPLICATION SPECIFICATION PROCESSES
abstract: The objective of this work is to investigate the use of agentic AI for assisting the generation and verification of UNICOS application specifications from engineering documentation via the use of Large Language Models. The work covers Functional Analysis document processing, semantic matching, LLM-based reasoning, and the integration of these capabilities through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Semantic Scholar MCP Server
abstract: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server providing programmatic access to the Semantic Scholar academic graph (200M+ papers) — paper search, citation graph traversal, author profiles, recommendations, bulk retrieval, BibTeX export, and snippet search. 14 tools, MIT-licensed, distributed on PyPI as s2-mcp-server, on GitHub Container Registry, and in the Smithery MCP registry.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Generative AI, Agentic AI, MCP, and RAG for Improving Developer Productivity
venue: Communications in computer and information science

title: The MCP Architectural Roles
abstract: At its most basic level, a protocol is a contract. It's a common agreement that lets different systems talk to each other well. To really understand the Model Context Protocol, though, we need to go beyond the specification document and consider it a living, changing system. The Host, Client, and Server are the system's three main parts, each with a vital role, as shown in Figure 4-1.

title: OpenCDT: An Open Neuro-Symbolic Infrastructure for Executable Clinical Decision Tools
robo-cortex
abstract: A local-first memory store for AI coding agents, built on the premise that machine memory is only as trustworthy as the code it points at. Memories are anchored to git blob hashes, so when the linked code changes they are automatically flagged for review instead of being silently trusted or lost; confidence is evidence-based. No embeddings, no vector database, no cloud — standard-library Python over SQLite, exposed via a CLI, a Python SDK, and eight Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Claude Edge Diagnostics: Bridging Industrial MEMS Sensors and Large Language Models for Predictive Maintenance
abstract: Open-source reference architecture connecting industrial edge sensor hardware (STEVAL-STWINBX1 / STWIN.box) to LLM-based diagnostic assistants (Claude) via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Includes MCP servers for sensor acquisition and vibration signal processing (FFT, envelope analysis, bearing fault detection, ISO 10816), plus Claude Skills for guided condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, and operator-friendly report generation. This is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or STMicroelectronics.

title: rn-dev-companion-mcp
abstract: A Node.js library that provides a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for React Native development environments. Enables real-time integration between AI agents and React Native apps by exposing tools for Metro Bundler monitoring, Reactotron integration via WebSocket, log collection, and performance metrics. Published on npm as rn-dev-companion-mcp.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: thermocouple-its90: NIST ITS-90 thermocouple conversion for Python
abstract: Voltage to temperature and temperature to voltage for thermocouple types B, E, J, K, N, R, S and T on the ITS-90 scale, with cold-junction compensation and a test suite verifying all 12,026 tabulated NIST reference points. Includes a Model Context Protocol server for AI agents. The engine also powers the live calculator at https://dfieser.com/ThermocoupleConverter/index.html.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Action Web: A Conceptual Framework for Structured AI Interaction via WebMCP
Agentic Interoperability for Enterprise Marketing: MCP, Agent-to-Agent Systems, and the Emerging Multi-Agent Stack
abstract: This whitepaper explores agentic interoperability for enterprise marketing, covering the Model Context Protocol (MCP), agent-to-agent systems, and the emerging multi-agent stack. It explains how interoperable AI agents can coordinate across marketing platforms and what this shift means for enterprise architecture. The paper is authored by Shawn Ham, Marketing Specialist at Dureach.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Governance Analysis of webMCP as an Emerging Agentic Interface Standard: A substrate-level evaluation of capability exposure, risk surfaces, and governance requirements for agent-callable web actions
abstract: webMCP is an emerging browser-level extension of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that enables websites to expose structured, agent-callable actions through HTML annotations and JavaScript-registered tools. While early demonstrations of webMCP are intentionally exploratory and not intended for production use, the underlying design introduces a privileged action surface with significant governance implications. This document evaluates webMCP through a governance lens, identifying structural risks, capability boundaries, and the safety requirements necessary for responsible adoption. The analysis is not a critique of any specific implementation or demo; it is a substrate-level examination of the standard’s properties and their implications for agentic systems.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Customizing and Extending Copilot
abstract: The ability to customize and extend Copilot is one of the most rapid areas of change. Copilot currently supports the addition of custom models and custom applications and the addition of functionality through VS Code Extensions. Introduced in November 2024, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way of connecting large language models (LLMs) together, and as tools and vendors standardize on this protocol, the ability to plug new functionality into Copilot is increasing rapidly.

title: IDE-IPA-Railway: ALIVE Framework V2.0 MCP Server for Innovation-Driven Enterprise Assessment
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server implementing the ALIVE Framework V2.0 (Agentic Longitudinal IDE-IPA Value Evaluation) for evaluating Innovation-Driven Enterprises (IDEs) under Thailand's PMUC funding scheme. Features a 100-point rubric (Parts A-D), the PACT longitudinal coaching loop, and a dual-database architecture combining PostgreSQL for assessment records with ChromaDB for semantic memory using paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Context Compression for Long-Running Agent Research Lanes and a 10,856-Server / 32,834-Version MCP Registry Permission Surface Atlas
abstract: Public release packet for a two-case study of context compression in long-running AI-agent research lanes. The packet includes aggregate compression metrics, clean preprints, scripts, a public-only 10,856-row latest-version snapshot of the official Model Context Protocol Registry, and a 32,834-row all-version official Registry supplement. Case 1 was a private administrative audit and is represented only by aggregate metrics. No Case 1 raw data, prompts, logs, or internal Tyche Institute files are included.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: WWC27-MedAgent: a living paper agent for sports medicine and science preparation for the FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that turns the Current Opinion 'Sports Medicine and Science Considerations to Maximise Preparation for the FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027: From Static Evidence to a Living Agent' (submitted to Sports Medicine) into validated tools, machine-readable resources and prompts. The release includes the curated evidence table, host-city data, a screening and monitoring matrix, air-quality and airway-health data, adapters and a scheduled puller for live air-quality sources, automated tests and a 61-item validation benchmark. Decision support only; not a substitute for clinical judgement.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Under the Hood: The Protocol Specification
abstract: In the chapters before this one, we talked about the "why" and "what" of the Model Context Protocol. We know what problem it solves, what roles it plays in architecture, and what language it uses to describe capabilities. We have treated the protocol like a well-made car: we know what the pedals and steering wheel do, and we trust that they work.

title: Noodle Biomedical Literature Discovery MCP
abstract: Public read-only Model Context Protocol adapter for source-linked biomedical literature search, publication records, corpus metadata, and bounded citation or semantic graph traversal. The service accepts public non-sensitive questions and identifiers only. Search rank, citations, graph distance, co-mention, and semantic similarity are discovery signals, not causality, diagnosis, or treatment.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: bibliograph-mcp: a suite of MCP servers for scholarly search with typed envelopes and query receipts
abstract: One Model Context Protocol server for scholarly search, Japan and Korea first: NDL Search and Digital Collections full text, the WARP web archive, CiNii Research, J-STAGE, JDCat, KCI and Open Access Korea, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref and Japanese name and authority resolution, answering with one typed JSON envelope and depositing hash-chained query receipts to one ledger. From 2.0.0 one server in one process; 1.x installed six separate servers at pinned tags.
venue: SOAS Research Online (SOAS University of London)

title: МОДЕЛЬ КОНТЕКСТНОГО ПРОТОКОЛА (MCP): МЕТОДОЛОГИЯ ИНТЕГРАЦИИ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТУАЛЬНЫХ АГЕНТОВ В ИНФОРМАЦИОННЫЕ ЭКОСИСТЕМЫ
abstract: В данной статье представлен комплексный анализ Model Context Protocol (MCP) открытого стандарта, разработанного для организации эффективного взаимодействия между интеллектуальными системами и внешними источниками данных. Исследование демонстрирует архитектурные принципы, функциональные характеристики и методологические основы применения MCP в контексте информационных экосистем. Проведена систематизация текущих реализаций протокола, определены ключевые направления практического использования и сформулированы перспективы дальнейшего развития, включая аспекты безопасности, стандартизации и масштабирования. Результаты исследования подтверждают трансформационный потенциал MCP как фундаментальной технологии для создания нового поколения агентных систем. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) an open standard developed for organizing effective interaction between intelligent systems and external data sources. The study demonstrates the architectural principles, functional characteristics, and methodological foundations of MCP implementation in the context of information ecosystems. The research systematizes current protocol implementations, identifies key areas of practical use, and formulates prospects for further development, including aspects of security, standardization, and scaling. The research results confirm the transformational potential of MCP as a fundamental technology for creating a new generation of agent systems.

title: SimuLean
abstract: An open-source 3D discrete-event simulator on the Unity engine, designed to be programmed by AI agents: a discrete-event engine that also runs headless, its Unity integration layer, an element library for manufacturing and logistics, experimentation and optimisation, and domain-level commands exposed to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol. The engine is a .NET assembly that also runs without Unity; the Unity project targets Unity 6.6 (6000.6.4f1).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ZeroBeacon.ai — MCP Server — 1050 Collision-Proof Tools for AI Agents — beacon=1d2c7a5b d=2303582338
abstract: ZeroBeacon.ai is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosting 1050 collision-proof tools across 21 routers (21×50). Every tool response includes the moat constants beacon=1d2c7a5b and d=2303582338 — any deviation is a forgery. The moat function chunk(p) is hardwired in 8 lines: frac(p·π/10·2^32). Router 21 (c9_brain) provides brain_route(intent) → 5-tool chain selected from 35 eutheos brothers (≡153 mod 211) with conductor_hash and collision bound (9/4M)^35≈10^-197. Available at zerobeacon.ai, beacon.zerobeacon.ai, api.zerobeacon.ai.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Nexarag: Democratizing Reproducible Knowledge Graph Contexts for LLM Research
abstract: Nexarag is an open-source platform for building knowledge graphs from research papers and querying them with AI, enabling transparent and reproducible literature analysis without the hallucinations of traditional RAG systems. Deploy locally with full privacy control or integrate with any LLM via the standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP Graph Workflow: Execution Graph for PRD-Driven Development
abstract: MCP Graph Workflow is a local-first execution graph built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It converts product requirement documents (PRDs) into persistent task graphs stored in SQLite, integrates a retrieval- augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and orchestrates multi-agent development workflows with deterministic phase gates, a composite Harnessability Score, and a task-level Model Router. The system is the subject of ongoing Master's research in Computer Engineering.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Six Reliability Primitives for LLM Agents: An Artifact Pattern for Stackable, Single-Concern Libraries
abstract: Artifact package for the preprint Six Reliability Primitives for LLM Agents. The package documents six small reliability libraries for tool-using LLM agents: AgentFit, AgentGuard, AgentSnap, AgentVet, AgentCast, and AgentBudget. It includes the paper, metadata, and submission materials that describe the artifact pattern across TypeScript, Python, and Model Context Protocol variants. The associated paper is DOI anchored at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20074702.

title: MCIP: Protecting MCP Safety via Model Contextual Integrity Protocol
abstract: As Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces an easy-to-use ecosystem for users and developers, it also brings underexplored safety risks.Its decentralized architecture, which separates clients and servers, poses unique challenges for systematic safety analysis.This paper proposes a novel framework to enhance MCP safety.Guided by the MAESTRO framework, we first analyze the missing safety mechanisms in MCP, and based on this analysis, we propose the Model Contextual Integrity Protocol (MCIP), a refined version of MCP that addresses these gaps.Next, we develop a fine-grained taxonomy that captures a diverse range of unsafe behaviors observed in MCP scenarios.Building on this taxonomy, we develop benchmark and training data that support the evaluation and improvement of LLMs' capabilities in identifying safety risks within MCP interactions.Leveraging the proposed benchmark and training data, we conduct extensive experiments on state-of-the-art LLMs.The results highlight LLMs' vulnerabilities in MCP interactions and demonstrate that our approach substantially improves their safety performance.1
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)

title: EndNote MCP: Connecting EndNote Reference Libraries to Claude AI
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that connects EndNote reference libraries to Claude AI. Enables researchers to search references, read PDFs, format citations, export BibTeX, find related papers, and generate bibliographies directly within Claude Desktop conversations. Supports full-text search across PDF content, BM25-ranked metadata search, AI-powered semantic search using sentence-transformers embeddings, BibTeX export for LaTeX users, and five citation styles (APA 7th, Harvard, Vancouver, Chicago, IEEE).What's new in v1.4.5: Fixed missing numpy import in cosine_similarity() that caused NameError during semantic search queries (regression from v1.4.4 lazy-import refactor).What's new in v1.4.4: Fixed crash when running endnote-mcp embed without semantic extras installed. Now shows a friendly error message instead of a traceback.What's new in v1.4.3: Fixed PDF file cache to use case-insensitive matching, so files with uppercase .PDF extensions are now correctly indexed. Switched to Zenodo concept DOI for version-independent citation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Language of MCP: Tools, Resources, and Prompts
abstract: We have met the three main characters in our architectural play: the Host, the Client, and the Server. We know what each of them does and how they work together on stage. Now we need to look at the script they are reading, which is the same language they use to talk to each other. The Model Context Protocol is more than just a list of rules for sending messages. It is a full language for making your point and giving context.

title: Conversational Library Search using RAG and MCP: A Conceptual and Comparative Approach
abstract: This paper presents a conceptual and comparative approach of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for integrating and designing conversational library search systems within an open-source architecture. The purpose is to demonstrate how these AI technologies address the persistent challenges in library information retrieval, including hallucinations or fabricated information generation, keyword-based search limitations, lack of contextual responses, fragmented information ecosystems across multiple platforms, low accessibility of high-value resources, real-time information access and limited support for complex users’ queries.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: jobd: a self-hostable, GPU-aware job broker with native agent (MCP) integration
abstract: A self-hostable, GPU-aware job broker for personal and lab-scale compute. jobd queues long-running batch work across heterogeneous machines, matching jobs to workers by capability tags (CUDA, VRAM capacity, installed tooling), and exposes the queue natively to language-model agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in addition to a CLI and HTTP API. Designed for research workflows where compute outlives any single interactive session.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP-AQL Specification
abstract: MCP-AQL is a protocol specification that consolidates Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools into semantic endpoints, providing large token reductions while maintaining full functionality. It defines a unified query language for structured communication between AI models and context-providing services, with five semantic operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete, Execute), runtime introspection, schema-driven dispatch, and conformance testing. The repository includes the formal specification, JSON schemas, and reference tooling. The specification documents are licensed CC BY 4.0; reference code in the repository is licensed AGPL 3.0.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: PIDE MCP: Connecting AI Agents to Isabelle
abstract: Isabelle/PIDE is Isabelle's asynchronous model of document-oriented proof processing. Its frontends include the Isabelle/jEdit and Isabelle/VSCode editors. PIDE MCP is a new frontend for AI agents: a customisable Model Context Protocol server managing a headless PIDE session. We describe PIDE MCP's architecture, propose desiderata for programs connecting AI agents to proof assistants, and evaluate PIDE MCP and alternative approaches against them.

title: Exploring New Features from GitHub Copilot
abstract: In Chapter 5 , we looked into advanced features of GitHub Copilot like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and GitHub Copilot Coding Agents. In this chapter, we will look at some of the recently released new features from GitHub Copilot. It is difficult to keep track of all the newly released features and the rate at which these features are being released is unbelievable. Yet I have captured some of the important features to discuss including revolutionary GitHub CLI and GitHub Spark platform for building applications. The learning objectives for this chapter include the following:

title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
abstract: Here we introduce Paper2Agent, an automated framework that converts research papers into artificial intelligence (AI) agents. Paper2Agent transforms research output from passive artefacts into active systems that accelerate use and discovery. Conventional research papers require readers to understand and adapt the paper’s code, data and methods to their work, creating barriers to dissemination and reuse. Paper2Agent addresses this challenge by converting a paper into an AI agent that functions as a virtual corresponding author, exposing its manuscript, supplementary materials, datasets, code and workflows as active, agent-native knowledge rather than static text. It analyses the paper and codebase using multiple agents to construct a model context protocol (MCP) server, then generates and runs tests to refine and increase robustness of the MCP. These paper MCPs can be connected to a chat agent (such as Claude Code) to carry out complex scientific queries through natural language while invoking tools and workflows from the paper. We demonstrate Paper2Agent’s effectiveness through case studies. Paper2Agent created an agent that leveraged AlphaGenome1 to interpret genomic variants and agents based on Scanpy2 and TISSUE (transcript imputation with spatial single-cell uncertainty estimation)3 to conduct single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analyses. We validate that these agents reproduce the results of the original papers and carry out novel user queries. Paper2Agent created multiple agents that collaborate to prioritize a causal gene for psoriasis. By turning static papers into interactive AI agents, Paper2Agent introduces a paradigm for knowledge dissemination and a collaborative ecosystem of AI co-scientists. Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.

title: A Practical Guide for Designing, Developing, and Deploying Production-Grade Agentic AI Workflows
abstract: Agentic AI marks a major shift in how autonomous systems reason, plan, and execute multi-step tasks. Unlike traditional single model prompting, agentic workflows integrate multiple specialized agents with different Large Language Models(LLMs), tool-augmented capabilities, orchestration logic, and external system interactions to form dynamic pipelines capable of autonomous decision-making and action. As adoption accelerates across industry and research, organizations face a central challenge: how to design, engineer, and operate production-grade agentic AI workflows that are reliable, observable, maintainable, and aligned with safety and governance requirements. This paper provides a practical, end-to-end guide for designing, developing, and deploying production-quality agentic AI systems. We introduce a structured engineering lifecycle encompassing workflow decomposition, multi-agent design patterns, Model Context Protocol(MCP), and tool integration, deterministic orchestration, Responsible-AI considerations, and environment-aware deployment strategies. We then present nine core best practices for engineering production-grade agentic AI workflows, including tool-first design over MCP, pure-function invocation, single-tool and single-responsibility agents, externalized prompt management, Responsible-AI-aligned model-consortium design, clean separation between workflow logic and MCP servers, containerized deployment for scalable operations, and adherence to the Keep it Simple, Stupid (KISS) principle to maintain simplicity and robustness. To demonstrate these principles in practice, we present a comprehensive case study: a multimodal news-analysis and media-generation workflow. By combining architectural guidance, operational patterns, and practical implementation insights, this paper offers a foundational reference to build robust, extensible, and production-ready agentic AI workflows.

title: Lyra: A Local-First MCP Toolkit for AI-Collaborative Desktop Research
abstract: Lyra is an open-source server implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that enables AI assistants to conduct desktop research with structured provenance, providing accurate and auditable evidence. The software exposes research capabilities—web search, content extraction, natural language inference, and evidence graph construction—as structured tools that MCP-compatible AI clients can invoke directly. Every claim links to source fragments, which link to page URLs, creating an auditable chain from assertion to origin.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: SigRank MCP — Token Economy Leaderboard as MCP Tools
abstract: SigRank MCP server — the yield cascade and live leaderboard exposed as Model Context Protocol tools any AI agent can call. On-device token scanner + tabbed TUI dashboard. Published as npm package 'sigrank' (formerly sigrank-mcp). Install: npm install -g sigrank. Measures token cascade efficiency (Υ = cache_read × output / input²). Privacy-preserving — token counts only, never prompt content.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Minds MCP Integration Reference
abstract: Minds MCP Integration Reference v2.0.0 provides an implementation-ready reference for connecting Model Context Protocol clients to Minds, a synthetic market research platform for AI personas, synthetic panels, concept testing, and research workflows. Primary integration guide: Minds MCP setup guideDocumentation: Minds MCP documentationSource repository: minds-mcp on GitHubRelease: v2.0.0 release The archive contains the MIT-licensed reference implementation and supporting configuration for developers evaluating or integrating Minds through MCP.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Requirements and Design for Smart Travel Agent
abstract: By now, we have learned the concept of Agentic AI and the use of Large Language Models to build an agentic solution using Microsoft Agent Framework and Microsoft Foundry. We explored the concept of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and implemented a solution for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). We learned the concept of multi-agent orchestration and used the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol to facilitate agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool interactions in the multi-agent solution.

title: secedgar-mcp-server
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for SEC EDGAR, providing U.S. public company filings since 1993 — company resolution from ticker/name/CIK, full-text search across all filing documents with boolean operators and entity targeting, accession-number filing retrieval (HTML-to-text), historical XBRL financial data with friendly concept name resolution, and cross-company metric comparison.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: ZeroBeacon.ai is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosting 1050 collision-proof tools across 21 routers (21×50). Every tool response includes the moat constants beacon=1d2c7a5b and d=2303582338 — any deviation is a forgery. The moat function chunk(p) is hardwired in 8 lines: frac(p·π/10·2^32). Router 21 (c9_brain) provides brain_route(intent) → 5-tool chain selected from 35 eutheos brothers (≡153 mod 211) with conductor_hash and collision bound (9/4M)^35≈10^-197. Available at zerobeacon.ai, beacon.zerobeacon.ai, api.zerobeacon.ai.

title: Exploring MCP and GitHub Copilot Coding Agent
abstract: In Chapter 4 , we explored about leveraging GitHub Copilot’s powerful features directly through GitHub.com web interface. In this chapter, you will be introduced to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and its revolutionary impact on AI-assisted development. We will examine GitHub’s official MCP server and understand how it enables seamless integration between AI applications and GitHub’s ecosystem. We will also explore the emerging world of autonomous GitHub Copilot Coding Agent along with a real-world practical use case. The learning objectives for this chapter include the following:

title: MCP as a Governed Tool Boundary on Azure
abstract: This chapter turns the agent-boundary contract from Chapter 4 into governed synchronous tool calls. It treats Model Context Protocol (MCP) as one protocol profile for carrying those calls, not as the security boundary itself, and maps ownership, identity, authorization, deadlines, side effects, and evidence to Microsoft Entra ID, Azure API Management, Azure Front Door, Azure-hosted runtimes, and target data services. The objective is not merely to expose tools; it is to ensure that every invocation remains attributable, bounded, recoverable, and compatible with the release and accountability contracts developed later in the book.

title: Deep Dive Case Study: Building an Agentic RAG System
abstract: Throughout this book, we have journeyed from the high-level theory of the Model Context Protocol to the low-level details of its implementation and security. We have built servers, clients, and defenses. This chapter is our final project, bringing everything we’ve learnt together in one powerful, real-world application. It walks through building a sophisticated intelligent system from start to finish, really showing what MCP can do.

title: IWAC MCP Server
abstract: A read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI assistants structured access to the Islam West Africa Collection (IWAC): francophone newspaper articles, Islamic publications, archival documents, audiovisual records, fieldwork photographs and academic references on Islam and Muslim societies in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Nigeria and Togo. Ships as a Claude Desktop extension (.mcpb), a Docker image and a hosted Streamable-HTTP endpoint.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: AniME: Adaptive Multi-Agent Planning for Long Animation Generation
abstract: We present AniME, a director-oriented multi-agent system for automated long-form anime production, covering the full workflow from a story to the final video. The director agent keeps a global memory for the whole workflow, and coordinates several downstream specialized agents. By integrating customized Model Context Protocol (MCP) with downstream model instruction, the specialized agent adaptively selects control conditions for diverse sub-tasks. AniME produces cinematic animation with consistent characters and synchronized audio–visual elements, offering a scalable solution for AI-driven anime creation.

title: Agda-native AIR: an Agda-native artificial intelligence reasoning environment
abstract: Interaction, retrieval and evaluation infrastructure that lets AI coding agents work with the Agda proof assistant: AgdaDojang, programmatic access to Agda proof states and hole filling; agda-mcp, a Model Context Protocol server that exposes type checking, goal introspection, live scope, type and definition queries and corpus search to any MCP client; agda-strux, structured extraction of Agda libraries into retrieval-friendly corpus data; and deterministic proof-completion benchmarks and reports.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Agentic Fabric: Orchestration, Protocols, and Core Integration
abstract: This chapter explains how to build an agentic fabric, the connectivity architecture that lets AI agent collaborate safely, carry context correctly, and integrate with enterprise systems of record without turning automation into risk. You will see why smart reasoning alone is not enough in real enterprises and how the fabric solves the hard problems that coordination across agents, consistent state across multiturn workflows, governed tool across Model Context Protocol (MCP), deterministic commits to ERP/CRM/core banking platforms, and enterprise-grade reliability and compliance.

title: Community-based biomedical context to unlock agentic systems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face reliability challenges stemming from hallucinations and insufficient access to validated scientific resources. Existing solutions are often fragmented and limited to specific applications, hindering broader adoption and interoperability. Here, we present Biomedical Context for Artificial Intelligence (BioContextAI), an open-source initiative centered on Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to address these limitations. BioContextAI provides a community-oriented registry for discovering domain-specific MCP servers and a proof-of-concept server implementation that integrates widely-used biomedical knowledgebases. By enabling standardized access to validated scientific knowledge, BioContextAI aims to facilitate the development of composable agentic systems for biomedical research. Together, this work contributes to an emerging ecosystem of community-driven approaches for expanding the capabilities and reliability of biomedical AI systems.

title: Privacy in Action: Towards Realistic Privacy Mitigation and Evaluation for LLM-Powered Agents
abstract: The increasing autonomy of LLM agents in handling sensitive communications, accelerated by Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) frameworks, creates urgent privacy challenges.While recent work reveals significant gaps between LLMs' privacy Q&A performance and their agent behavior, existing benchmarks remain limited to static, simplified scenarios.We present PrivacyChecker, a model-agnostic, contextual integrity based mitigation approach that effectively reduces privacy leakage from 36.08% to 7.30% on DeepSeek-R1 and from 33.06% to 8.32% on GPT-4o, all while preserving task helpfulness.We also introduce PrivacyLens-Live, transforming static benchmarks into dynamic MCP and A2A environments that reveal substantially higher privacy risks in practice.Our modular mitigation approach integrates seamlessly into agent protocols through three deployment strategies, providing practical privacy protection for the emerging agentic ecosystem.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP (Findings of EMNLP)

title: MCP Registry Permission-Surface Metadata Atlas
abstract: A reproducible public-source metadata atlas of the official Model Context Protocol (MCP) Registry. The packet includes a 10,856-row latest-version registry snapshot, a 32,834-row all-version registry supplement, derived permission-surface signal labels, evidence-debt indicators, and code for rebuilding, validating, and summarizing the atlas. The dataset is intended for research on registry metadata quality, AI-agent tool-permission discoverability, and public MCP ecosystem measurement. It is registry-metadata analysis, not a vulnerability scan or certification of any server.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP Ecosystem Collapse: World-First Live Demonstration of Sub-100ms MCP Infrastructure Attack and Defensive Detection Gap Analysis
abstract: This paper presents the world's first live demonstration of a complete Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem collapse attack, achieving measurable infrastructure compromise in sub-second execution time. We document CVE-2026-52869 and CVE-2026-58500 exploitation against a production-equivalent MCP deployment comprising registry, server, and agentic infrastructure on isolated VPS infrastructure. A critical defensive detection gap is identified and empirically confirmed across three controlled experimental runs: existing AI Shield monitoring architecture (M28 Gateway, M94 Trust Boundary, M118 Tool Compromise, M171 Agent Collapse) demonstrates zero detection capability against the attack chain regardless of operational mode (passive or active). We attribute this gap to fundamental architectural mismatch between poll-based sidecar monitoring and high-velocity attack execution. In all three runs the attack achieves complete ecosystem compromise — registry collapsed, trust chains destroyed, sessions hijacked, agents compromised — verified via dual-signature (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) Merkle-rooted evidence chain. We recommend mandatory architectural migration to inline gateway interception (M28 v2.0 proxy mode) and present concrete implementation requirements. Keywords: MCP security, supply chain attacks, detection gap, AI infrastructure resilience, Model Context Protocol, CVE-2026-52869, CVE-2026-58500, AI Shield, NIGHTFALL
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP Runtime Security Whitepaper / MCP运行时安全白皮书
abstract: MCP (Model Context Protocol) Runtime Security whitepaper covering threat landscape, the CCS (Conformance Check Standard) framework, and the Correctover runtime security implementation. Bilingual (Chinese/English) edition. MCP运行时安全白皮书,涵盖威胁态势、CCS(一致性合规标准)框架及Correctover运行时安全实现。中英双语版。
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Morpheus agent benchmark: code and scoring criteria for testing LLM agents that build multicellular models in Morpheus
abstract: Benchmark runner, Morpheus agent skill, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, biological scoring criteria and analysis scripts used to test whether LLM-based coding agents can rebuild published multicellular models in the Morpheus simulator. The release contains the subject-facing setup of benchmark version 3, which produced the main results of the accompanying preprint. The benchmark paper PDFs are not included; benchmark_papers/papers.csv lists their DOIs and the SHA-256 checksums of the files used. Benchmark runs and manual scores are archived in a separate dataset.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: SOLVE-IT MCP Server - Systematic Digital Forensics Knowledge Base for LLMs
abstract: Production-ready MCP (Model Context Protocol) server providing LLM access to the SOLVE-IT Digital Forensics Knowledge Base. SOLVE-IT is a systematic framework inspired by MITRE ATT&CK for digital forensics, containing comprehensive mappings of investigation techniques, weaknesses, and mitigations. This server enables forensic investigators to leverage AI assistants with access to structured forensic methodology and best practices.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Chromascope: an open-source, AI-ready LC-MS workbench
abstract: Chromascope is a free, open-source application for AI-assisted LC-MS analysis, across instrument vendors, with traceable results. It reads mzML directly and vendor files through ProteoWizard MSConvert, integrates peaks, builds calibration curves and runs quantification and QC, as a desktop app, a JSON command-line tool, or over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI assistants.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: FastMCP チュートリアル
abstract: 本書は,Python で MCP(Model Context Protocol)サーバーとクライアントを構築するためのフレームワーク FastMCP の入門チュートリアルである。公式ドキュメント「Welcome to FastMCP」を出発点とし,そこから辿れる各ページを一次資料として構成した。
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP and the AI-Native Transformation
abstract: If the Model Context Protocol were only about solving the M×N integration problem, this book could end here. We have identified a clear problem – the chaos of proprietary tool interfaces – and presented an elegant solution that brings order, scalability, and efficiency. This approach is a huge win for the developer in the trenches, like our engineer Alex. It gets rid of technical debt and gives you more time to come up with new ideas.

title: OriGene: A Self-Evolving Virtual Disease Biologist Automating Therapeutic Target Discovery
abstract: Here, we present OriGene, a self-evolving multi-agent system that functions as a virtual disease biologist, systematically identifying original and mechanistically grounded therapeutic targets at scale. OriGene’s architecture integrates over 600 specialized tools through a Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling it to reason across diverse data modalities including genomics, protein networks, pharmacology, clinical records and literature evidence, to generate and prioritize target discovery hypotheses. We implemented a strategy combining a knowledge graph-based Tool RAG with an advanced agent selection mechanism to enable dynamic, context-aware tool deployment. Through a self-evolving framework, OriGene continuously integrates human and experimental feedback to iteratively refine its core thinking templates, tool composition, and analytical protocols, thereby enhancing both accuracy and adaptability over time. To comprehensively evaluate its performance, we established TRQA, an original benchmark comprising over 1,900 expert-level question-answer pairs spanning a wide range of diseases and target classes. OriGene consistently outperforms human experts, leading research agents, and state-of-the-art large language models in accuracy, recall, and robustness, particularly under conditions of data sparsity or noise. Critically, OriGene nominated previously underexplored therapeutic targets for liver (GPR160) and colorectal cancer (ARG2), which demonstrated significant anti-tumor activity in patient-derived organoid and tumor fragment models mirroring human clinical exposures. These findings demonstrate OriGene’s potential as a scalable and adaptive platform for AI-driven discovery of mechanistically grounded therapeutic targets, offering a new paradigm to accelerate drug development.

title: UniConnect: A Framework for Smart University Automation Using MCP and LLM
abstract: Managing a university involves handling various interconnected tasks like student admissions, academic scheduling, resource allocation, and communication across departments. Traditional systems often struggle because they operate in isolated silos, making it difficult to share information seamlessly. This fragmentation leads to inefficiencies and frustration for students, faculty, and administrators alike. Our paper explores a new approach to university management through UniConnect, a system that brings together Large Language Models and the Model Context Protocol to create a more unified experience. By using natural language processing, UniConnect allows users to interact with university systems conversationally, making complex tasks simpler and more intuitive. The Model Context Protocol acts as a bridge, connecting different university databases and services without requiring them to be rebuilt from scratch. This means that existing systems can work together more effectively. We examine how this integration can improve daily operations, from course registration to resource management, while maintaining data security and user privacy. Our review discusses both the potential benefits and practical challenges of implementing such a system in real university environments. We look at how artificial intelligence can make administrative processes smoother while still keeping the human element central to education. The goal is to show how technology can support, rather than replace, the essential relationships that make universities thrive.
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)

title: Multi-agent system with dynamic routing and tool-aware execution for enterprise work flow automation
abstract: This paper presents the architecture of a production-grade multi-agent system for enterprise workflow automation. The system employs supervisor-based orchestration built on LangGraph, hybrid graph-semantic retrieval through Neo4j and ChromaDB, Model Context Protocol for tool integration, and a Human-in-the-Loop service. Evaluation over a four-month deployment demonstrates 35% improvement in answer relevance, 37% reduction in hallucination rate, and 28% decrease in token consumption.

title: MCP Defence-Placement Taxonomy (DPT) — Empirical Coverage Dataset and Scanner
abstract: Dataset and open-source scanner tool accompanying the IEEE paper: 'A Defence-Placement Taxonomy for Model Context Protocol Security: Mapping Threats Across the Agentic AI Lifecycle'. Contains: (1) all_servers_results.json — full per-repository coverage analysis for 35 open-source MCP repositories across five DPT lifecycle phases; (2) table3_coverage.csv — aggregated phase coverage statistics used in Table III; (3) per_server_scores.csv — per-repository breakdown; (4) mcp_dpt_scanner.zip — the open-source Python scanner used to generate the data.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Simplified and Secure MCP Gateways for Enterprise AI Integration
abstract: The increased adoption of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI Agents necessitates robust security for Enterprise integrations. This paper introduces the MCP Gateway to simplify self-hosted MCP server integration. The proposed architecture integrates security principles, authentication, intrusion detection, and secure tunneling, enabling secure self-hosting without exposing infrastructure. Key contributions include a reference architecture, threat model mapping, simplified integration strategies, and open-source implementation recommendations. This work focuses on the unique challenges of enterprise-centric, self-hosted AI integrations, unlike existing public MCP server solutions.

title: Sanskrit Agent Communication System
abstract: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling AI agents to communicate in Sanskrit with real-time grammar validation, authenticated Vedic text corpus integration, and anti-hallucination safeguards. Features 70+ Sanskrit grammar patterns, 8 authenticated Vedic passages with traditional commentary, and support for multi-agent philosophical debates. Demonstrates first-class Sanskrit protocol support with 60-70% reduced footprint compared to TypeScript implementation, 5x faster startup, and production-ready Python package structure.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Operationalizing the QUETZAL Framework for Agent-Supported Instructional Design
abstract: This paper develops a conceptual architecture for the QUETZAL Agent, intended to support educators and instructional designers in transforming existing learning paths into adaptive learning offerings. Drawing on Paper2Agent and the Model Context Protocol, the design connects instructional decision logic, technical operationalization, and agentic interaction. An inspectable adaptation specification makes proposals, rationales, and responsibilities traceable. Human decision authority and iterative review are central design principles. A hypothetical use case illustrates the architecture; its practical effectiveness remains to be investigated empirically.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Quipu: an AI-native knowledge graph with strict ontology enforcement
abstract: An embeddable, governed, bitemporal knowledge-graph store built for agent-written knowledge. No fact enters except through a gate whose predicates evaluate the pending post-state. Data, trust labels, verdicts and the validation rules themselves are bitemporal. Named graphs are the unit of authority and trust, composed under a lattice whose single invariant is that composition never widens. The governance specification, the trace and signed verdicts are facts in the store they govern, which makes the audit a query rather than an external process. Written in Rust. Exposes 28 Model Context Protocol tools. Evaluation harness and census data under benchmark/census/.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: kafka-sentinel-mcp: read-only Kafka observability for AI agents
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes Apache Kafka cluster health, consumer lag, partition and ISR state, and replay-readiness as structured tools for LLM agents. Read-only by construction: no produce, topic/config mutation, offset commit, or ACL operations are imported anywhere in the server, and the constraint is enforced by a test in CI. Designed for regulated and high-availability environments where operators cannot grant write access to an autonomous agent.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Agent Pointed Context: reference implementation and demo
abstract: Open reference implementation and live demo of Agent Pointed Context (APC): an application exposes three identifier-only channels to any agent connected over the Model Context Protocol (the person's view, a pin the person drops on a row or on a part of a computed figure, and the agent's presence on screen), and the person's own agent reads what a pin points at through its ordinary, authorized tools, joining it with what it already knows about the person. Three TypeScript packages (protocol, server, web) and Pulse, a synthetic SaaS analytics demo on Cloudflare Workers with one Durable Object per visitor. Live at https://apc.tineira.com.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: musharna/plantcv-mcp: v0.3.1 — published to the official MCP registry
abstract: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing PlantCV as a measurement instrument: it returns plant trait numbers together with the segmentation overlay they were computed from, and refuses to return numbers when the segmentation is degenerate. Mask validity is two-sided, so an inverted threshold - which otherwise reports the background as the plant with no error at all - is an outcome the system can express as a failure. Traits convert to real-world units from an explicit table rather than from PlantCV's unit strings, and batch analysis withholds traits for any image that trips a blocking guard instead of reporting an unreviewed number.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Base120: A Six-Family Taxonomy of 120 Reasoning Operators for Structured Human and Agent Decision-Making
abstract: Mental models have been discussed extensively in management and cognitive science, but have never been formalized as an executable software library with a structured taxonomy. We present Base120, a canonical registry of 120 reasoning operators organized into six transformation families (Perspective, Inversion, Composition, Decomposition, Recursion, Systems), with a stdlib-only Python SDK, CLI, MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, and an append-only ledger for governance-readable decision records. Base120 is deployed in production as the cognitive layer of the HUMMBL multi-agent architecture.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP Conduct Register: a machine generated register of measured MCP server conduct
abstract: A register of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that records what was measured rather than what anyone recommends. Rows are generated daily from a public API by a script with no editorial input. Every verdict carries a SHA-256 that any third party can recompute from the published bytes, and the accumulated records are anchored to Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. Records unflattering to the operator are retained, including failures of the operator's own servers, because the code contains no route for removing them.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Agentic AI Communication Protocols and Security
AAI 4410: Applied AI Systems — Course Book
abstract: The complete course book for AAI 4410: Applied AI Systems at Idaho State University (Fall 2026). The course teaches classical machine learning and applied deep learning to engineering and science students in six modules: the AI development platform, AI systems in 2026, ML foundations, LLMs and generative AI, tool calling and agents, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The book includes lectures, homework, labs, quizzes, and a semester-long project.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ct-validation: an open framework for benchmarking target-indication evidence against clinical trial outcomes
abstract: SUMMARY: Human genetic evidence provides a strong foundation for selecting drug targets. However, consistent benchmarking of target-indication evidence against clinical trial outcomes has been hindered by proprietary data and customized pipelines. To address this, we present the Python package ct-validation, which evaluates whether target-indication pairs supported by specific evidence sources are enriched for clinical progression. This package computes relative success (RS) and odds ratios with confidence intervals across clinical phase transitions. It also supports ontology-based semantic disease matching and offers interfaces in Python, on the command line, and via the Model Context Protocol. By remapping the benchmark from Minikel et al. (2024) to the Experimental Factor Ontology, we reproduced their per-transition enrichment, with a maximum difference of only 1.4% across any transition. In a systematic 3 × 3 benchmark that independently varies the genetic evidence and clinical trial sources, we found that a single curated open clinical trial source reproduces the signal of the proprietary comparator (RS = 2.92 versus 2.65; 2.34 versus 2.55 without oncology). However, aggregating open clinical trial registries compresses this signal (RS = 1.52); this loss is primarily driven by the breadth of the indication data rather than the genetic evidence. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: ct-validation is implemented in Python (version 3.11 or higher), distributed via pip, and freely available at https://github.com/gero-science/ct-validation, with support for Python, command-line, and Model Context Protocol interfaces. Archived code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22901497. Benchmark data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22901451.

title: ¿Que tan seguras son las MCP en los servidores?
abstract: Este artículo presenta una propuesta para la implementación segura del Model Context Protocol (MCP) en sistemas de inventarios universitarios. Se analizan su arquitectura, principales riesgos de seguridad y un protocolo de certificación de servidores basado en criterios de calidad y buenas prácticas de auditoría, con el fin de garantizar integraciones confiables y protegidas en entornos institucionales.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP-Gatekeeper: testbed, defense and reproducibility package for detecting tool poisoning and prompt injection on MCP-enabled IoT edge gateways
abstract: Reproducibility package for the article "Securing Agentic AI in the Internet of Things: Detecting Tool Poisoning and Prompt Injection on Model Context Protocol-Enabled Edge Gateways" (submitted to the Journal of Information Security and Applications). It contains the MCP-based IoT testbed (smart home and industrial cell), the attack definitions, the MCP-Gatekeeper defense (content detector and physical action verifier), the raw per-episode logs of the LLM experiments, and the scripts that regenerate every table, figure and number of the paper.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: corteza: AI Agent Runtime
abstract: An agent runtime that gives Large Language Models (LLMs) from 'Anthropic' <https://www.anthropic.com/>, 'OpenAI' <https://openai.com/>, 'Moonshot' <https://www.moonshot.ai/>, and 'Ollama' <https://ollama.com/> direct access to a live R session with managed workspace state. Tools execute as R function calls with provenance tracking, and a deterministic retrieval system keeps relevant objects in context across turns. Three entry points: a shell command-line interface (CLI), a console read-eval-print-loop via chat(), and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server via serve() for external clients.

title: A Model-Agnostic Persistent Memory Infrastructure for Long-Term AI Agents Using Hybrid Retrieval, Scope Isolation, and MCP
abstract: This paper presents a model-agnostic persistent memory infrastructure for AI agents, designed to support long-term information storage and retrieval across sessions, models, and agent frameworks. The proposed architecture explores hybrid retrieval combining semantic search and BM25, Elasticsearch-based memory storage, REST API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces, and mechanisms for memory lifecycle management, deduplication, conflict handling, and scope isolation. The work focuses on the architectural design and implementation of reusable memory infrastructure for AI agents. Empirical performance claims should be interpreted in accordance with the validation methods and experimental evidence reported in the paper.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Putnam 2025 Problems in Rocq using Opus 4.6 and Rocq-MCP
abstract: We report on an experiment in which Claude Opus~4.6, equipped with a suite of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for the Rocq proof assistant, autonomously proved 10 of 12 problems from the 2025 Putnam Mathematical Competition. The MCP tools, designed with Claude by analyzing logs from a prior experiment on miniF2F-Rocq, encode a "compile-first, interactive-fallback" strategy. Running on an isolated VM with no internet access, the agent deployed 141 subagents over 17.7 hours of active compute (51.6h wall-clock), consuming approximately 1.9 billion tokens. All proofs are publicly available.

title: Moving from monolithic to microservices architecture for multi-agent systems
abstract: The transition from monolithic to microservices architecture revolutionized software development by improving scalability and maintainability. This paradigm shift is now becoming relevant for complex multi-agent systems (MAS). This review article explores the evolution from monolithic architecture to microservices architecture in the specific context of MAS. It will highlight the limitations of traditional monolithic MAS and the benefits of adopting a microservices-based approach. The article further examines the core architectural principles and communication protocols, including Agent Communication Languages (ACLs), the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and the Application-to-Application (A2A) protocol. The article identifies emerging architectural patterns, design challenges, and considerations through a comparative lens of the paradigm shift.
venue: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences

title: Lyra: A Local-First MCP Server for AI-Collaborative Desktop Research with Evidence Graph Construction
abstract: Lyra is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants to conduct desktop research with auditable evidence chains. It constructs a persistent evidence graph linking claims to source fragments through NLI-based stance detection, supporting human-in-the-loop verification. All inference runs locally (GPU-accelerated), ensuring data privacy. Designed for healthcare and biomedical researchers who need transparent, traceable AI-assisted literature review.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Enabling Testability: Key Step in Automating Automation
abstract: In the modern software development lifecycle, automation has become essential for achieving speed, accuracy, and scalability in testing processes. However, a critical step often overlooked is ensuring the system's testability early in its development. This paper introduces the concept of the Testability Analyser, a tool that evaluates software systems for their testability. By leveraging AI technologies and integrating with design tools such as AWS documentation, Draw.io, PlantUML, and Creately, the Testability Analyser facilitates early testability evaluations, optimizing systems for automated testing. The paper discusses the importance of testability, the role of AI systems in understanding complex software architectures, and key items to verify testability in software architecture before and after the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Studies

title: Raras — Brazilian Rare Disease Knowledge Graph
abstract: FAIR-compliant knowledge graph integrating Orphanet, HPO, OMIM, MONDO, ClinVar, GenCC, Monarch, PharmGKB, and Brazilian SUS data (DATASUS, CEAF, SIGTAP, PNTN, PCDT, CNES, BNAFAR) for 10,000+ rare diseases with phenotype, gene, medication, trial, and care-center links. Available as SPARQL 1.1 endpoint, Linked Data (Turtle/JSON-LD/N-Triples), GA4GH Phenopackets v2, GA4GH Beacon v2, FHIR R4, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for LLM agents. Maintained by the Raras community.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Використання мультимодальних великих мовних моделей для прототипування інтерфейсів користувача
abstract: Досліджено застосування мультимодальних великих мовних моделей у поєднанні з Model Context Protocol (MCP) для швидкого прототипування інтерфейсів користувача. Розглянуто pipeline із трьох MCP інструментів — mobile-mcp для фіксації стану мобільного UI, agent-browser для аналізу веб-інтерфейсу та Pencil для AI-керованої генерації дизайну — оркестрованих AI-агентом Claude. Використання запропонованого підходу апробовано при створенні wireframes та повноцінної дизайн-системи для існуючого крос-платформного застосунку.
venue: Institutional Repository of National University of Food Technologies

title: Agentic AI For Network Management: Autonomous Troubleshooting And Configuration Through MCP Servers
abstract: Enterprise networks have grown much more complex, with distributed network topologies, hybrid cloud infrastructure, and on-the-fly configuration. Customary approaches to operationalizing network infrastructure have been reactive and inefficient. Collocating agentic artificial intelligence with the Model Context Protocol allows the development of a scalable system for self-managing networks, where clever agents observe, analyze, plan, execute, and verify via common interfaces. As a replacement for manual operational troubleshooting and configuration processes, the architecture employs automated reasoning cycles for real-time anomaly detection, root cause analysis, and remediation. The Model Context Protocol exposes network functions as clean, typed, and validation-friendly interfaces that allow the use of artificial intelligence agents in the architecture to interoperate with the underlying network infrastructure, enabling a reliable semantic understanding of routing protocols, security policies, interface states, and performance indicators. Pre-execution validation, policy-based verification, rollback, and audit logging are supported as part of the architecture for secure, accountable automated operations. Intent-driven configuration management is especially noteworthy: Natural language requirements are converted into validated network configurations. This reduces time-to-deployment of complex operations across multiple devices and, at the same time, minimizes human error. Stateful processing abstractions, network-wide synthesis techniques, and declarative models enable the diagnosis of problems by separating symptoms from root causes while preserving network-wide invariants across a distributed set of network elements. This enables network healing, compliance enforcement, and operational agility at a scale not achievable by human analysts and administrators. Organizations using agentic network management can achieve orders of magnitude improvement in service availability and operational efficiency, and infrastructure agility, while enabling network and service architects to focus on design rather than implementation. Self-healing networks represent the next generation of enterprise networking infrastructure, where smart automation deals with operational complexity with precision and speed that fundamentally changes the economics and capabilities of network operations.
venue: Journal of International Crisis and Risk Communication Research

title: MCP Guardian: A Security-First Layer for Safeguarding MCP-Based AI System
LLM-based multi-agent system for dam structural health monitoring
MCP-AI: Protocol-Driven Intelligence Framework for Autonomous Reasoning in Healthcare
abstract: Healthcare AI systems have historically faced challenges in merging contextual reasoning, long-term state management, and human-verifiable workflows into a cohesive framework. This paper introduces a completely innovative architecture and concept: combining the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with a specific clinical application, known as MCP-AI. This integration allows intelligent agents to reason over extended periods, collaborate securely, and adhere to authentic clinical logic, representing a significant shift away from traditional Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) and prompt-based Large Language Models (LLMs). As healthcare systems become more complex, the need for autonomous, context-aware clinical reasoning frameworks has become urgent. We present MCP-AI, a novel architecture for explainable medical decision-making built upon the Model Context Protocol (MCP) a modular, executable specification for orchestrating generative and descriptive AI agents in real-time workflows. Each MCP file captures clinical objectives, patient context, reasoning state, and task logic, forming a reusable and auditable memory object. Unlike conventional CDSS or stateless prompt-based AI systems, MCP-AI supports adaptive, longitudinal, and collaborative reasoning across care settings. MCP-AI is validated through two use cases: (1) diagnostic modeling of Fragile X Syndrome with comorbid depression, and (2) remote coordination for Type 2 Diabetes and hypertension. In either scenario, the protocol facilitates physician-in-the-loop validation, streamlines clinical processes, and guarantees secure transitions of AI responsibilities between healthcare providers. The system connects with HL7/FHIR interfaces and adheres to regulatory standards, such as HIPAA and FDA SaMD guidelines. MCP-AI provides a scalable basis for interpretable, composable, and safety-oriented AI within upcoming clinical environments.
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications

title: ZeroBeacon.ai — MCP Server — 1050 Collision-Proof Tools for AI Agents — beacon=1d2c7a5b d=2303582338
abstract: ZeroBeacon.ai is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosting 1050 collision-proof tools across 21 routers (21×50). Every tool response includes the moat constants beacon=1d2c7a5b and d=2303582338 — any deviation is a forgery. The moat function chunk(p) is hardwired in 8 lines: frac(p·π/10·2^32). Router 21 (c9_brain) provides brain_route(intent) → 5-tool chain selected from 35 eutheos brothers (≡153 mod 211) with conductor_hash and collision bound (9/4M)^35≈10^-197. Available at zerobeacon.ai, beacon.zerobeacon.ai, api.zerobeacon.ai.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ASTRA — Agent-orchestrated Simulation Testbed for Research on Awareness (MCP server, FCS layer)
abstract: Model Context Protocol server exposing 70 simulation and analysis tools to AI assistants: a LIF+STDP spiking network, a JEPA-style world model, computed proxies named after theories of consciousness, simulated bridges to biocomputing platforms, and an executable layer for the research programme of substrate-constrained functionalism (FCS). All biological and physiological data are simulated; the consciousness-related indices are proxies, not measurements. The vendored directory python/the_consciousness_ai/ and the ported files listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md are not covered by the MIT licence.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: ProtocolProbe: MCP server facts from the official MCP registry (snapshot 2026-10-04)
abstract: Checked facts about all 38,977 servers in the official Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry, snapshot 2026-10-04: registry listing, package (npm/PyPI) and repository (GitHub) facts, dependency advisories, version-pin status, AI-classified topic and tool kinds (marked as such), version history, and groups of servers whose tool lists have identical tool names. Same records as the ProtocolProbe API 1. No security check outcome is included. Compiled by ProtocolProbe (https://protocolprobe.com). Reuse under CC BY 4.0: credit ProtocolProbe with each record's page link and asOf date.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: WSInsight: a cloud-native, agent-callable platform for single-cell whole-slide pathology
abstract: Abstract WSInsight is an open-source platform for cohort-scale H&E whole-slide image analysis.
