This episode unpacks the $40,000 re-embedding nightmare one company faced, and explores three strategies to avoid it: event-driven re-embedding with PostgreSQL triggers, sidestepping embeddings entirely via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for structured data, and client-side embedding caching with TTLs for gradual, non-breaking migrations. We also cover the VICE scoring model for choosing between vector search and traditional search, why top coding tools have abandoned vector RAG for AST-based retrieval, and the hybrid patterns that combine BM25, vector similarity, and cross-encoders. Show Notes ## The Silent Failure of Embedding Deprecation When OpenAI deprecated its `ada-002` embedding model, one company faced a $40,000 bill — not from API costs, but from two weeks of developer time to re-embed their entire corpus. Worse, the replacement model produced different embedding dimensions and similarity scores, breaking their entire retrieval index. This isn't a crash; it's a slow, silent decay. Users don't complain about embeddings — they just stop trusting the chatbot. The core problem is that most teams don't measure retrieval quality. No precision@K, no NDCG, no confidence scoring. By the time someone traces bad answers back to stale embeddings, user trust is already gone. The LlamaIndex team explicitly calls out "embedding mismatch" as a primary silent failure mode, recommending that teams pin model versions and store model names in metadata for drift detection. ## Smarter Re-Embedding: Event-Driven Architecture Batch re-embedding is the brute-force fix: for 500,000 chunks, API costs are only $5. But during backfill, your index becomes partially stale — some chunks have new embeddings, others old — making retrieval quality worse during migration. Batch also treats all documents equally, re-embedding unchanged six-month-old content alongside freshly updated ones. The smarter approach is event-driven: use PostgreSQL triggers with a queue pattern (`SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`) to re-embed only when source data actually changes. Track `is_current` flags, `model_version` columns, and `source_hash` values for idempotent re-embedding. This reduces operational overhead but doesn't eliminate the fundamental lock-in to a specific embedding model. ## Can MCP Sidestep Embeddings Entirely? The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how LLMs discover and call external tools at runtime via JSON-RPC 2.0. Some claim MCP makes RAG obsolete, but AWS, Google Cloud, and Databricks all agree: MCP complements RAG, it doesn't replace it. For structured data — sales figures, database queries — MCP's dynamic querying is superior because you get exact, authoritative answers with no semantic fuzziness. But for unstructured prose like legal documents or support tickets, semantic search remains essential. The VICE scoring model (Value, Impact, Confidence, Effort) helps decide: score both traditional search and vector search across those dimensions. If one approach scores more than 2x the other, it's the clear winner. Within 2x, use a hybrid. For e-commerce product search, hybrid wins. For legal document discovery, pure vector search dominates. ## Client-Side Caching: Gradual Migration Caching embeddings client-side (e.g., in IndexedDB) with a TTL transforms model deprecation from a big-bang migration into a rolling transition. Old embeddings work locally until their TTL expires; new embeddings are fetched on refresh. Cold starts take 3-10 seconds, but warm queries hit 200-550ms — usable for interactive apps. The trade-off is managing cache invalidation, but it eliminates the two-week developer crunch and the partially-stale-index problem. ## The Real Principle: Match Retrieval to Data Structure Top coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor have largely abandoned vector RAG for code. They use grep, file tree inspection, AST-based navigation, and large context windows instead. Code has structure — import graphs, call chains, explicit references — and flattening it into embedding space destroys information. But you can't grep a million support tickets for "customer is frustrated about billing." The retrieval method must match the data structure: structured data → MCP-style querying; unstructured prose → vector search; everything in between → hybrid BM25 + vector similarity + cross-encoder re-ranking. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/embedding-deprecation-rag-fixes
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Programming a Biological Cell: a review
Hermes vs OpenClaw: Mobile-to-Server AI Frameworks
abstract: Episode summary: The Hermes agent framework is pulling developers away from OpenClaw at an accelerating rate. But beneath the surface question of which framework wins lies a harder problem: can you run complex, long development sessions with sub-agents and bash output from a mobile interface? This episode unpacks the three key reasons for the migration—development velocity, architectural flexibility, and native MCP support—and explores why neither framework has fully cracked the mobile-to-server interaction problem for serious development work. We also examine Nvidia's strategic investment in Hermes and what it signals about the emerging "agent runtime layer. Show Notes The Hermes agent framework has become the default recommendation for developers who want a self-hosted AI agent on their own infrastructure. Its rise comes at the expense of OpenClaw, the incumbent that dominated the personal agent space through early 2025. The migration is driven by three factors: Hermes ships features every few weeks while OpenClaw's development stalled for months; Hermes treats tools, memory backends, and the reasoning loop as composable components rather than a rigid architecture; and Hermes natively supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), letting developers plug in custom MCP servers with zero adaptation work. Nvidia's venture arm recently invested in the company behind Hermes, signaling confidence that the agent runtime layer will become a lasting category. The harder question is whether any framework can solve the mobile-to-server interaction problem for serious development work. The use case described—long coding sessions with delegation to sub-agents and bash output, accessed from a phone—remains unsolved. Hermes has a Telegram integration that works for simple queries like "check my inbox" but fails for multi-line code blocks and complex session management. Its web dashboard is still a desktop interface squeezed into a phone screen. The pragmatic answer may be to treat the phone as a control plane—start, monitor, and intervene in sessions—while reserving the full terminal experience for a workstation. Hermes supports this better than OpenClaw through structured status reporting and transparent agent state, but neither framework has fully cracked the problem. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/hermes-openclaw-mobile-server-ai
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Agentic and Generative AI for Intelligent Autonomous Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing: A Systematic Analysis
Advancing Secure Cognitive Automation in Upstream Operations: A Case Study on Artificial Intelligence Deployment Using CypherCrescent's SEPAL Enterprise Planning Solution (EPS)
abstract: Abstract The global energy sector is going through a big change from Industry 5.0, which focuses on people working together, to Industry 6.0, which is based on cognitive automation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a key part of making operations more resilient, streamlining workflows, cutting carbon emissions, while saving costs. International operators have shown that AI can cut seismic interpretation times by more than 90% and save an average of $38 million per asset per year in unplanned downtime costs. However, the roadmap for achieving these results in Africa's indigenous energy sector is still not well developed. This paper explores CypherCrescent Limited's strategic integration of AI, establishing a technical benchmark for digital transformation across Nigeria and Africa's energy value chain. We introduce a secure-by-design methodology for embedding AI into the SEPAL Enterprise Planning Solution (EPS), CypherCrescent's economic modeling and financial analytics platform. To address industry concerns about data sovereignty and model reliability, the implementation uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standard architectural layer. This method allows Large Language Models (LLMs) and proprietary legacy databases to interact in a controlled and governed way without revealing sensitive raw data. By incorporating MCP-compliant SDKs, the system supports physics-informed machine learning and Natural Language Processing (NLP) for contextual querying of long-term organizational datasets, inevitably advancing basic digitization to cognitive autonomy. Quantitative outcomes from these deployments indicate significant operational enhancements, including decreases in non-productive time (NPT) and optimised operational expenditure (OPEX). These results prove that AI can help improve asset safety and integrity while also dealing with problems with regional infrastructure. The paper also suggests a framework that can be used by other operators in Africa and can be adapted to their needs. It stresses the need to move from reactive legacy systems to predictive, data-driven ecosystems. This study also laid out a phased adoption strategy and strong data protection measures, giving a practical guide for how to meet ESG standards and stay competitive in the energy market in 2035. The findings emphasise that intelligent, autonomous, and secure operations are the "price of admission" for the future of energy.
venue: SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition

title: ЕВОЛЮЦІЯ ВИКОРИСТАННЯ СТАНДАРТІВ ЕЛЕКТРОННОГО НАВЧАННЯ XAPI ТА CMI5
abstract: У статті проведено системно-структурний аналіз розвитку і використання відкритого стандарту збору, зберігання та обміну даними про навчальний досвід користувачів – xAPI як ключового інструменту побудови сучасних відкритих освітніх екосистем, здатних забезпечувати збір і накопичення даних про навчання людини впродовж життя для їх подальшого аналізу з використанням технологій великих даних і штучного інтелекту. Проведено аналітичний огляд технічної документації та сучасних публікацій щодо останніх оновлень стандарту xAPI, розробки його нових профілів, а також результати реалізації проєкту CATAPULT, спрямованого на прискорення впровадження стандарту cmi5. Розглянуті аспекти практичного використання стандарту, зокрема наведено огляд доступних програмних засобів для збору даних xAPI-відстеження відео, соціальних мереж і відеоконференцій та їх зберігання в Learning Record Store (LRS). Основну увагу приділено розв’язанню проблеми «семантичного розриву» між сирими даними в LRS та інтелектуальними модулями підтримки навчання завдяки інтеграції стандарту xAPI з новітнім протоколом Model Context Protocol (MCP), що дає змогу великим мовним моделям та ШІ-агентам інтерпретувати контекст діяльності учня в реальному часі. Описано приклад багаторівневої архітектури системи, яка містить Activity Providers (професійно орієнтоване ПЗ), семантичний міст на базі MCP-сервера та спеціалізованих ШІ-оркестраторів. У ній динамічний стан учня (DLS) розглядається як багатофакторна модель, що інтегрує показники поточної продуктивності, когнітивного навантаження та моделей поведінки. Такий підхід дає змогу трансформувати освітню аналітику з інструменту ретроспективної звітності на активний механізм педагогічного супроводу. Розкрито сутність стратегії «Just-in-Time Scaffolding», за якої автономне втручання системи (коригувальний, проактивний або метакогнітивний зворотній зв’язок) ініціюється на основі предиктивного аналізу траєкторії дій учня. У висновках систематизовано прикладні переваги впровадження xAPI для основних стейкхолдерів: від персоналізації досвіду здобувачів освіти до валідації професійної майстерності для роботодавців.

title: Intelligent Systems for Secure Digital Enterprises
abstract: The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity, distributed architectures, intelligent automation, digital twins, machine learning, and enterprise analytics has fundamentally transformed the operational landscape of modern digital enterprises. Organizations increasingly depend on intelligent systems to automate business processes, strengthen cyber resilience, optimize financial decision-making, improve software engineering practices, and support real-time operational intelligence. Despite significant technological advances, enterprises continue to face persistent challenges related to cybersecurity risks, heterogeneous cloud infrastructures, governance complexity, scalability limitations, ethical AI deployment, regulatory compliance, and sustainable digital transformation. Existing studies frequently investigate these domains independently, resulting in fragmented knowledge that limits the development of integrated enterprise intelligence frameworks. This review synthesizes contemporary research concerning intelligent systems for secure digital enterprises by examining advances in AI-driven decision support, intelligent cybersecurity, cloud-native computing, DevOps automation, digital twin technologies, financial technology, enterprise governance, predictive analytics, and intelligent resource optimization. The study adopts a structured qualitative review methodology based exclusively on the provided literature and develops a unified conceptual framework that explains interactions among enterprise intelligence, secure infrastructure, adaptive automation, governance mechanisms, and operational resilience. The review demonstrates that intelligent enterprises increasingly rely on interconnected AI services supported by scalable cloud infrastructure, policy-driven cybersecurity, continuous monitoring, intelligent orchestration, explainable decision-making, and autonomous optimization. Emerging technologies including digital twins, generative AI, Model Context Protocol (MCP), multi-agent AI, predictive machine learning, sentiment analytics, and event-driven architectures significantly improve enterprise responsiveness while introducing new governance and security requirements. The findings further indicate that enterprise resilience depends not solely on technological sophistication but also on organizational leadership, secure software engineering practices, regulatory compliance, and human-centered operational models. The proposed integrated framework contributes to the growing body of enterprise intelligence research by connecting technological innovation with governance, operational resilience, and secure digital transformation. The review provides practical guidance for researchers, enterprise architects, policymakers, and organizational leaders seeking to develop scalable, secure, and intelligent enterprise ecosystems capable of supporting future digital economies.
venue: Ethiopian International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research

title: GeoAI-THM Studio v0.1.0: an agent that builds and runs verified subsurface heat, flow, deformation and transport models with OpenGeoSys, with code, verification record and technical notes
abstract: GeoAI-THM Studio is a free, noncommercial agent that turns a plain-language request (English or Korean) into an OpenGeoSys 6.5.8 model of subsurface heat conduction, groundwater flow, heat transport, solute transport, consolidation, thermal stress or coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical processes, runs it, and reports values computed from the run, checking each number in the answer against the run, the model inputs and the request. The language model edits a typed model tree through tools ordered by a state machine; a translator writes the OpenGeoSys input; a configuration is computed only after its verification cases have passed with the installed versions; and an output guardrail rejects answers whose numbers cannot be traced to the run, the model inputs or the request. This record contains: (1) the source code of the geoai-thm-studio Python package 0.1.0 (command-line chat, Model Context Protocol server, tools, translator, mesh step, verification cases, examples, instructions and knowledge base) with its tests; (2) the verification record of 27 cases against exact solutions, official OpenGeoSys benchmarks and, for a demonstration configuration, consistency checks (21 within 1 %, all within 2.5 %); (3) the scenarios, scripts and result files of the tests with small language models (a Claude Haiku stand-in and a final check with gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-terra), the recomputation audit and the point-source element-size sweep; (4) the technical note in English and Korean (PDF); (5) the preprint prepared for the ESS Open Archive (PDF, the version of this release); (6) the installable wheel geoai_thm_studio-0.1.0. Install: pip install "geoai-thm-studio[mesh-gmsh] @ git+https://github.com/geoaialignment/geoai-thm-studio@v0.1.0" (supported: macOS 15 or later on Apple Silicon, Python 3.12; experimental: Linux x86_64, tested so far only under emulation). The software is free for noncommercial use, but the chat agent calls the OpenAI API with the user's own key, and OpenAI bills those calls to the user's account. Repeat the verification with thmstudio verify; the scripts in scripts/ rebuild every reported number from results/ and runs/. Results are for learning and first estimates, not for design, licensing or safety assessments. Licences: code PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; documentation, examples, verification reports and technical notes CC BY-NC 4.0 (see LICENSE and LICENSE-docs.md). Commercial use is not permitted. OpenGeoSys (BSD 3-Clause) and Gmsh (GPL, run only as a separate program) keep their own licences and are not redistributed.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Dynamic Context Quality Index (d-CQI): Self-Describing Semantic Data Contracts and Temporal Boundary Enforcement for Autonomous Agentic Data Meshes Vaibhav
Evaluating AI Agents on a Mechanical Repair Procedure: Head Gasket Bench
abstract: We present Head Gasket Bench, an interactive benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can execute a cylinder-head gasket replacement on a 1990s 1.6 L SOHC inline-four engine via an 18-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. Built over a 1,255-body CAD assembly with 626 reinstallation rules, 100 attachment restorations, and 14 service-manual entries, the benchmark enforces access dependencies, tool selection, surface preparation, metrological thresholds, spiral torque sequences, and valve timing. Runs are graded on 12 binary checkpoints (18 points) by two independent evaluators: an in-process runtime grader and an offline transcript scorer, which agree 100 percent across 13 reference and fault trajectories spanning five variants (V1--V5). We report three empirical cohorts totaling 35 episodes on the standard job (V1): (1) three single-agent Codex CLI runs (GPT-6-Astra, GPT-6-Luna, GPT-6.1-Sol), scoring 15/18, 13/18, and 3/18; (2) eight single-agent Claude Code runs, where all five claude-opus-5-5 runs score 16/18 (mean 383.4 calls, USD 9.19 cost), failing only the final checkpoint because separate remove-and-install gasket calls leave an atomic replacement predicate unmet and block 100 attachment restorations, while three claude-haiku-5-5 runs score 14/18, 12/18, and 12/18; and (3) a 24-run multi-agent study comparing single agents, native subagents, and two Fleet topologies across two rounds. After Round 1 (8 runs) exposed a worker-finish hazard and one boundary discrepancy, Round 2 (16 runs) enforced a lead-only finish grant with 16/16 scorer agreement, and the 1+4 Fleet arm achieved the first two full 18/18 repairs (mean 12.75/18 vs. 5.75/18 for single agents).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Context-Enforcement Network Engine for Decentralized Data Meshes: A Kernel-Grounded Control Plane for Autonomous Agents
VectraYX-Nano: A 42M-Parameter Spanish Cybersecurity Language Model with Curriculum Learning and Native Tool Use
abstract: We present VectraYX-Nano, a 41.95M-parameter decoder-only language model trained from scratch in Spanish for cybersecurity, with a Latin-American regional focus and native tool invocation via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The model has four contributions. (i) Corpus: VectraYX-Sec-ES, a 170M-token Spanish corpus assembled by an eight-VM distributed pipeline at ~$25 USD of cloud compute and split into three curriculum phases (conversational 42M, cybersecurity 118M, offensive tooling 10M). (ii) Architecture: a 42M Transformer decoder with GQA, QK-Norm, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE and z-loss, paired with a domain-balanced 16,384-token byte-fallback BPE. (iii) Curriculum with replay across the three phases yields a monotonic loss descent (9.80 -> 3.17 -> 3.00 -> 2.16); after SFT (loss 1.74) the v2 bootstrap-ablation reference attains a conversational gate of 0.775 +/- 0.043 on B5 over N=4 seeds, and a controlled Phase-2 replay sweep over {0,5,10,25,50}% saturates B5 at >=25% replay. (iv) Two empirical findings, both N=4. A controlled bootstrap-corpus ablation across v2 (OpenSubs), v4 (mC4-ES), and v6 (60/25/15 OpenSubs/mC4/Wiki) exposes a loss-versus-register inversion: lower-perplexity bootstraps yield measurably worse conversational behavior (v2 > v4 > v6 on B5 at every paired seed). The B4 (tool-selection) floor of 0.000 is a corpus-density artifact, not a capacity gate: rebalancing the SFT mixture to tool-use ratio 1:21 yields VectraYX-Nano v7, the released headline configuration, reaching B4 = 0.230 +/- 0.052 at 42M while retaining B1 = 0.332 +/- 0.005 and B5 = 0.725 +/- 0.130; a LoRA replication on a 260M from-scratch mid-tier reaches 0.445 +/- 0.201. The released GGUF is 96 MB in F16, runs sub-second TTFT on commodity hardware under llama.cpp, and is, to our knowledge, the first published Spanish-native cybersecurity LLM with end-to-end MCP integration.

title: EmDash 初心者向け利用ガイド
abstract: EmDash は、Cloudflare が 2026 年に発表したフルスタック・サーバーレス TypeScript CMS(コンテンツ管理システム)であり、WordPress の設計思想を現代的な Web 技術で再構築した「WordPressの精神的後継者」と位置づけられている。Astro フレームワークを基盤とし、Cloudflare Workers 上でサーバーレスに動作する。各プラグインを独立した V8 isolate 内でサンドボックス実行することで、WordPress で深刻な課題であったプラグイン起因のセキュリティ脆弱性を根本的に解決している。また、MCP(Model Context Protocol)サーバーの内蔵、Agent Skills、CLI ツールにより、Claude Code をはじめとする AI エージェントからのプロンプト指示によるサイト構築・コンテンツ管理を可能にしている点も大きな特徴である。 本書は、EmDash をこれから利用する初心者を対象とした利用ガイドである。技術アーキテクチャの概要、インストールから基本設定、コンテンツ管理・メディア管理・テーマ開発・認証といった日常的な利用方法、プラグインシステム、デプロイ、WordPress からの移行手順、AI ツールとの統合機能、マネタイズ機能までを体系的に解説する。付録として Cloudflare アカウントの開設方法および EmDash 本体の開発環境構築手順も収録した。
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: α 3 -Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents Over 6G Networks
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as high-level controllers for autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) missions. However, current evaluations rarely assess whether such agents remain safe, protocol-compliant, and effective under realistic constraints of next-generation networking. This paper introduces $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench, a benchmark for assessing LLM-driven UAV autonomy as a multi-turn conversational reasoning and control problem operating under dynamic 6G conditions. Each mission is modelled as a language-mediated control loop between an LLM-based UAV agent and a human operator, where decisions must satisfy strict schema validity, speaker alternation, mission policies, and safety bounds while adapting to fluctuating network slices (URLLC/eMBB/mMTC), latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, and edge-load variations. To reflect modern agentic workflows, $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench integrates a dual-action layer that supports both Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) coordination, enabling the evaluation of tool-use consistency and multi-agent interactions within UAV missions. We construct a large-scale corpus of 113k AI conversational episodes grounded in UAVBench scenarios and evaluate 17 state-of-the-art LLMs using a fixed subset of 50 episodes per scenario under deterministic decoding. We propose a composite $\alpha ^{3}$ metric that unifies six pillars—Task Outcome, Safety Policy, Tool Consistency, Interaction Quality, Network Robustness, and Communication Cost—with reliability- and efficiency-normalized scores per second and per thousand tokens. Experimental results show that several frontier models achieve near-perfect mission success and safety compliance (Task Outcome and Safety Policy $\geq 0.95$ ), yet their robustness and efficiency diverge substantially: under degraded 6G conditions, Network Robustness scores drop by up to 30–40%, while efficiency-normalized performance varies by more than a $2\times $ factor across models in both $\alpha ^{3}$ per-second and $\alpha ^{3}$ per-1k-tokens metrics, reflecting significant variance in inference latency and token consumption. $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench provides a reproducible, extensible foundation for benchmarking conversational UAV autonomy and guiding the development of safe, network-aware, and resource-efficient LLM agents in 6G-enabled aerial systems. To support open science and reproducibility, we release the $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench dataset on GitHub: https://github.com/maferrag/AlphaBench
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: A Contemporary Approach to Platform Synergy: Structured Context Sharing, Programmatic Connectivity Layers, and the Advancement of Intelligent Autonomous Systems
abstract: The rapid evolution of intelligent autonomous systems has intensified the need for interoperable, context-aware, and scalable digital infrastructures capable of supporting cross-platform intelligence exchange. This paper examines a contemporary architectural paradigm for platform synergy grounded in structured context sharing and programmatic connectivity layers, emphasizing their role in enabling next-generation autonomous systems. The central thesis argues that the convergence of deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-driven decision systems, modular interoperability frameworks, and standardized context protocols significantly enhances system adaptability, scalability, and operational coherence across heterogeneous environments. Recent advancements in intelligent transportation systems (ITS), autonomous mobility networks, and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) highlight the importance of structured communication layers for distributed intelligence coordination. Studies on DRL-based traffic control and mobility optimization demonstrate how adaptive policy learning improves real-time system responsiveness (Aradi, 2022; Liang et al., 2019). Similarly, urban air mobility frameworks introduce multi-layered orchestration challenges that necessitate unified data-sharing architectures (Wang et al., 2023). However, these systems remain fragmented due to the absence of standardized interoperability protocols capable of maintaining contextual integrity across distributed agents. This research integrates insights from autonomous system design, neuromuscular control modeling, and human-centric decision frameworks to conceptualize platform synergy as a multi-layered construct. Drawing on interoperability advancements such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), APIs, and agentic AI frameworks, the study emphasizes the role of structured context propagation in enabling seamless cross-system coordination (Venkiteela, 2025). MCP-based architectures, in particular, demonstrate potential in standardizing context exchange between heterogeneous agents, thereby reducing computational redundancy and improving system-level coherence. Through a critical synthesis of existing literature and architectural analysis, the paper identifies key gaps in current autonomous system design, particularly in contextual fragmentation, lack of semantic interoperability, and limited cross-domain adaptability. The proposed framework outlines a structured connectivity model that bridges these gaps by aligning DRL-based decision layers with context-aware interoperability protocols. The findings suggest that platform synergy, when supported by structured context sharing and programmatic connectivity layers, significantly enhances the efficiency, resilience, and scalability of intelligent autonomous systems. The study concludes by highlighting future research directions in scalable agentic architectures, real-time interoperability governance, and adaptive context orchestration mechanisms.
venue: International Journal of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Research

title: Agent-First Backends: No Dashboard Required
abstract: Episode summary: What if you never logged into a dashboard again? This episode explores agent-first development — designing systems where AI agents, not human clicks, are the primary interface. We built a podcast project with no admin backend: just an API, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and Claude Code. The experience reveals a future where you type a sentence and your CRM, ERP, or CMS updates instantly. But there's a catch: identity and authorization haven't caught up. With 81% of teams past the planning phase but only 14.4% having full security approval, the dual-track reality is already here. We dig into what best practices look like for distributed agent use in team environments — and why the next bottleneck isn't the AI, it's the auth layer. Show Notes Agent-First Backends: What Happens When the Dashboard Disappears** Imagine running your entire podcast management system — updating episode descriptions, changing categories, publishing — without ever opening a browser. No login screen. No menu navigation. No save button. Just tell an agent what to do, and it happens. That's not a hypothetical. We built it. **The Core Idea: Agent-First Development** Agent-first development means designing a system where the primary interface is an AI agent, not a human clicking through a GUI. The API becomes the real product. The agent discovers available operations, understands their schemas, and executes them based on natural language instructions. In our podcast project, there is no admin panel. There's a front end for listeners, an API serving episode data, and Claude Code connected through MCP (Model Context Protocol) with defined skills: "edit episode title," "update description," "publish episode." I type a sentence, and the episode updates. Compare that to WordPress: four clicks, a scroll, and waiting for page loads just to change a category. The agent-first approach eliminates that friction entirely. **The Hidden Benefit: Lowering the Quality Threshold** The most overlooked effect isn't just convenience — it changes what you bother to do. When a four-click workflow exists, you might skip updating a description or fixing a small error. When it's one sentence, you just do it. The threshold for maintaining quality drops to zero. **The Current Limitation: Desktop-Only** Right now, Claude Code runs in your terminal on your laptop. You can't pull out your phone and update an episode while walking to get coffee. Skills don't sync across surfaces — Claude Code skills are filesystem-based and separate from Claude.ai skills. But this limitation is temporary. Anthropic's agent SDK and OpenAI's Agents SDK are adding remote execution. Composio already handles OAuth lifecycle with 850+ SaaS integrations. By late 2026, agents will be embeddable in Slack, mobile apps, and browser extensions. **The Real Bottleneck: Identity and Authorization** The single-user case is solved. But what happens with a team of five editors, where one can publish and two can only draft? The agent needs to carry identity context through every operation. The numbers are alarming. Gravitee's State of AI Agent Security report found only 21.9% of teams treat AI agents as independent, identity-bearing entities. 45.6% still rely on shared API keys for agent-to-agent authentication. 27% use custom hardcoded authorization logic. Shared API keys mean the agent operates with a master key. If multiple people use it, there's no way to tell who did what. **The Dual-Track Reality** Daniel's prediction holds: agent-first becomes the standard way to interact with business systems, but organizations won't delete their backends overnight. Traditional dashboards become debugging tools and audit log viewers. The dual track is already the messy present — 81% of teams are past planning, but only 14.4% have full security approval. **What's Next** The identity layer is catching up. NIST launched an AI Agent Standards Initiative focused on agent identity and authorization. An IETF draft called AI-Auth addresses agent authorization with federation support. Until those standards mature, anyone building agent-first systems is rolling their own auth patterns — fine for a two-person podcast project, terrifying for a regulated enterprise. The bottleneck isn't the agent technology. It's the auth layer. And that's where the real design work begins. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/agent-first-backends-no-dashboard
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Zero-Trust Identity for Autonomous AI Agents: Unifying SPIFFE, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, OIDC, and OPA in Multi-Agent Architectures
abstract: The rapid adoption of autonomous AI agents in distributed microservices architectures introduces a critical and largely unsolved security challenge: how to establish, verify, and enforce identity across every layer of an agentic workflow. In traditional systems, identity management addresses two well-understood dimensions: human user identity (authenticated via passwords, single sign-on, or multi-factor mechanisms) and a limited number of service identities (managed through static API keys or long-lived service accounts). These approaches suffice when services execute predetermined logic on behalf of known callers. However, the emergence of agentic workflows, where autonomous agents reason, invoke tools, and chain multi-step actions across service boundaries, fundamentally changes the identity landscape. Each agent workload requires its own cryptographically verifiable workload identity, and the system must maintain governed identity propagation that securely carries both the originating user’s authorization context and the calling service’s identity through every hop of the request chain, all while preserving secure session state across process boundaries and service restarts. Moreover, just as APIs are classified into public, protected, and private tiers with progressively stricter access controls, agents must be similarly classified: public agents accessible to any authenticated user, protected agents restricted to users with specific roles, and private agents accessible only through authorized internal services with both valid user credentials and verified workload identity. We present AgentSecurity, a production-ready framework that unifies three complementary standards to achieve zero-trust identity with governed identity propagation for multi-agent systems: (1) OAuth 2.1 with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) for secure human authentication via OpenID Connect (OIDC), with disk-persisted session state that survives process restarts, eliminating authorization code interception attacks; (2) SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs (JSON Web Token-based SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Documents) for cryptographic workload identity, replacing heavyweight X.509 mutual TLS (mTLS) with lightweight, audience-scoped, short-lived JWTs that give every agent its own verifiable identity; and (3) the Open Policy Agent (OPA) for declarative, two-dimensional authorization that jointly evaluates user roles and caller service identity in a single policy decision, ensuring that identity propagation is governed at every trust boundary. We demonstrate this framework on a real multi-agent platform comprising LangGraph agents orchestrated via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), where every inter-service call carries both a user identity token and a workload identity token, propagating the user’s authorization context through the entire agentic pipeline. Every access decision is governed by auditable, version-controlled Rego policies. Our evaluation shows that the framework adds less than 12 ms of latency overhead per request while providing four independent authentication layers, fail-closed authorization, and automatic credential rotation. A complete reference implementation is available at https://github.com/krishna1501/AgentSecurity.
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology

title: Teaching SQL with an Agentic LLM: A Fifteen-Category Hallucination Taxonomy and Context-Pack Mitigation Strategy for Claude Sonnet 5
abstract: Text-to-SQL generation with large language models (LLMs) is increasingly used in database teaching, yet it remains susceptible to hallucination: the production of syntactically valid but referentially or semantically incorrect queries. This paper proposes a working taxonomy of fifteen hallucination categories in text-to-SQL generation, spanning schema-referential errors, join and cardinality errors, aggregation-grain errors, linguistic ambiguity, dialect and type misuse, NULL and temporal-logic errors, and higher-order failure modes such as explanation-query inconsistency, fabricated execu- tion results, and false security assumptions. Each category is illustrated with a natural-language request and a corresponding hallucinated query against a common PostgreSQL schema, together with a targeted mitigation. Mitigations are organized into two complementary layers: a context pack supplied once by the instructor (schema DDL, column catalog, foreign-key graph, and a set of standing rules) and an agentic execute-observe-correct loop, formalized here through explicit definitions of "generation" and "session", in which an assistant such as Claude Sonnet 5 issues queries against a live PostgreSQL database via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), inspects the returned rows or errors, and revises the query before presenting it to the user. The paper provides a recap table of categories and countermeasures, intended as a practical checklist for instructors and students applying agentic LLMs to SQL laboratory training. The taxonomy is positioned against related error classifications from the text-to-SQL and broader LLM-hallucination literature, showing convergence on schema- and logic-level categories while identifying conversational and pedagogical failure modes – ambiguity, car- dinality fan-out, explanation inconsistency, fabricated results, and security over-confidence – that fall outside the scope of static, benchmark-based taxonomies. The paper argues that the fifteen categories are structural properties of schema-grounded SQL generation and therefore model-agnostic, while their frequency and severity are expected to vary across model tiers and context pack quality. The paper concludes by highlighting three avenues for future research: extending the empirical material to schemas of realistic industrial scale; a classroom deployment study comparing learning outcomes with and without the proposed mitigations; and a sampling-based characterization of hallucination frequency and robustness across repeated and adversarial prompting.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Safety for MCP Database Servers
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly granted direct access to enterprise data systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This makes it possible for end-users to query operational databases in plain language and receive immediate, contextual answers. Such capabilities promise to democratize analytics and accelerate decision-making, but they also introduce a new class of high-consequence risks. A model can misinterpret ambiguous intent, overreach its role by touching unauthorized tables, or be coerced by carefully crafted prompts into revealing schema information or issuing destructive commands. In high-stakes domains such as finance, healthcare, or critical infrastructure, these risks are unacceptable without additional safeguards. In this work, we present a practical human-in-the-loop (HITL) safety layer designed specifically for MCP database servers. Our interceptor examines every SQL query generated by an LLM and assigns a risk score using a combination of lightweight heuristics (e.g., keyword patterns, schema sensitivity) and a calibrated machine-learning classifier. Queries deemed low risk are executed immediately to preserve responsiveness. Those in an intermediate “gray zone” are paused and surfaced to a reviewer through a lightweight web interface, while queries that match hard-deny patterns (e.g., destructive DROP or mass DELETE without predicates) are blocked outright. Reviewer outcomes—approve, modify, or reject—are continuously logged and fed back into the model, allowing the system to adapt and reduce unnecessary escalations over time. We evaluate the approach on a dataset of approximately 25,000 SQL-like queries (sql_- risk.csv), encompassing benign analytics, inadvertent model errors, and adversarial promptinjection attempts. Across thresholds, the hybrid system achieves 89–95% accuracy and maintains near-perfect recall for destructive queries, while reducing human intervention rates from roughly 20% at cold start to 7–10% with adaptation. Beyond quantitative results, we document case studies illustrating how the system intercepted schema exfiltration attempts, role overreach, and silent mass-update errors. We also provide an operational playbook, discuss ethical and privacy implications, and release reproducibility artifacts for community use. Our findings suggest that HITL checkpoints, when carefully engineered, can serve as a practical guardrail for deploying LLM agents in production data environments.

title: Desarrollo de Agentes Autónomos IA de Ingeniería Inversa
abstract: La ingeniería inversa se erige como un pilar crítico y de alta complejidad dentro del ecosistema de la ciberseguridad contemporánea, resultando indispensable para el análisis de código malicioso y la auditoría de software de código cerrado. El presente trabajo aborda la necesidad estratégica de automatizar estos procesos mediante arquitecturas de orquestación agéntica para mitigar la extenuante carga de trabajo manual que tradicionalmente recae sobre el analista. El estudio se centra en la evaluación técnica del protocolo Model Context Protocol (MCP) como estándar de interacción entre modelos de lenguaje (LLM) y las herramientas de ingeniería inversa radare2 y Ghidra, comparando la precisión operativa de diversos stacks tecnológicos para identificar configuraciones óptimas de autonomía. Con el propósito de contrastar la hipótesis de viabilidad, el diseño metodológico se estructuró sobre un entorno experimental controlado en Kali Linux, apoyado por un oráculo de validación determinista. A través de un benchmark de 10 desafíos de dificultad incremental aplicados a cinco modelos de lenguaje pertenecientes a diferentes familias (DeepSeek, GPT, Claude...), los resultados permitieron validar empíricamente la superioridad del stack GPT 5.3 Codex + GhidraMCP. Esta combinación demostró un dominio técnico sobresaliente, alcanzando métricas del 90% de éxito en “pass@3”. Los hallazgos permiten determinar que la arquitectura agéntica se define no solo como una herramienta de soporte, sino como un multiplicador estratégico colaborativo que reduce significativamente la carga cognitiva en tareas de desofuscación repetitivas, potenciando exponencialmente la velocidad de respuesta ante incidentes críticos.

title: Sovereign Connector Framework (SCF): Homeostatic Security Boundaries for Personal AI Agents
abstract: AbstractThe Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, has rapidly becomethe de facto standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data sources. Wedocument 25 security vulnerabilities inherent to MCP's architecture—not as implementationdefects, but as predictable consequences of a convenience-first design philosophy thatrecapitulates the confused deputy problem at unprecedented scale. We propose the SovereignConnector Framework (SCF), an independent architectural framework founded on homeostaticprinciples drawn from cardiac physiology and ecological systems theory. SCF introduces fiveSCF Preprint v1.2 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | Page 2Sovereign Connector Framework (SCF) SymbioMind Research Practiceinterlocking mechanisms: semantic sandboxing via formal grammar constraints on individualoperations, homeostatic drift detection modeled on cardiac arrhythmia monitoring to addresssequential composition risks, a 24±6 month pattern-lock on framework specifications (aprincipled design choice, not a derived parameter), a physical sovereignty switch implementedin RISC-V open hardware, and the LoopGuard open-source middleware enforcing HATI(Honest, Accurate, Transparent, Insightful, Impact) constraints on all connections. We evaluateboth protocols using the HATI rubric, yielding scores of 67/100 (MCP) and 93/100 (SCF).Critically, we document five failure modes that SCF cannot prevent—including userdependency atrophy, state-level supply chain compromise, catastrophic compression loss, afailed capability-based design approach, and the composition spectre (sequential operationrisks that grammar constraints alone cannot address)—treating these as primary intellectualassets rather than deficiencies. This v1.1 revision incorporates findings from a three-evaluatorreview protocol (sympathetic, adversarial, and naive), with corrections and additions explicitlyattributed to the review process. We conclude with more questions than answers, proposing thata framework which can scale to billions of users without friction is, by definition, incorrectlydesigned.Keywords: AI safety, connector frameworks, homeostatic security, semantic sandboxing, ModelContext Protocol, sovereign computing, HATI evaluation, failure-first design, personal AI agents
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
Context Rot and MCP Tool Attrition in Production-Scale Codebases: An Empirical Investigation of Context-Driven Tool Calling Degradation in Agentic AI Coding Systems
Intelligent virtual assistant for business data access
abstract: Modern organisations increasingly struggle to access and interpret enterprise data that is dispersed across isolated Business Information Systems (BIS). These silos hinder the ability to obtain a unified view of information, which is essential for timely and informed decisionmaking. Advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer the possibility of querying such data in natural language, thereby lowering the technical barrier for business users. However, the adoption of these models in corporate environments is constrained by concerns over data privacy, regulatory compliance, and the high operational costs of cloud-based solutions. These challenges underline the need for on-premises, resource-efficient approaches that preserve control over sensitive information. This dissertation presents an intelligent virtual assistant that answers business questions by orchestrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools to inspect schemas, draft explicitprojection SQL, validate read-only execution, and ground responses in results from a local Microsoft SQL Server instance of AdventureWorksDW2022. No model fine-tuning is performed; instead, the approach combines runtime schema filtering, deny-list validation, and prompt scaffolding to minimise hallucinations and enforce governance. A controlled evaluation over 52 representative prompts compares three configurations: a prompt-only baseline (B0), MCP with unfiltered schemas (B1), and a curated setup with filtering and explicit projections (S). The curated configuration yields substantially higher execution accuracy and fewer schema-error incidents than both baselines, demonstrating that governed tool use materially increases correctness without relaxing the privacy posture on a single on-premises workstation. Latency observations are reported descriptively and are attributable primarily to model generation rather than orchestration. These findings support the feasibility of privacy-preserving, on-premises conversational analytics under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), and suggest practical next steps: broadening schema coverage, refining curation policies, and exploring lighter local models and decoding strategies to improve interactivity.
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)

title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
abstract: AI agents now pause for approval before they send money, delete files or email outsiders, and that approval is usually treated as a second factor. We argue it is one only when compromising the agent cannot produce it and when it names exactly what it approves, and we test both conditions. We define twelve attacks on the approval path, including decoy recipients, amount cancellation, card padding, label spoofing, enrollment squatting and threshold splitting, and run them against the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), the Microsoft action-bound approval design and Model Context Protocol (MCP) elicitation. An audit of ten agent runtimes finds no third-party verifiable approval record, no flood limits where measurable, and post-approval argument changes in four of eight runtimes with measurable binding. As a reference defense we build ASU (Agent Step-Up), a gateway that renders the approval card from a canonical effect descriptor, has a passkey on the phone of the user sign its digest, and executes only the stored call. Tamarin proves its binding, single-use and key-level non-repudiation properties under three stated hypotheses (53 lemmas). Across 27,108 scripted trials and 609 AgentDojo attack pairs, ASU stops substitution, replay and grant stretching, and the trusted card cuts forged-narration attack success from 0.54 to 0.03. With 15 current language models as automated approvers, the trusted card raises the attack catch rate from 0.30 to 0.98, at the cost of refusing 16 percent of harmless near misses, mostly due to a placeholder artifact in our stimuli. A second device adds nothing measurable over a trusted on-host confirmation in these experiments, flooding still succeeds 0.45 to 0.60 of the time against a modeled approver, and approval cannot stop effects that policy already allows. Code, data and proofs: https://github.com/Sports-Vision-Inc/agent-step-up

title: Diseño e implementación de un agente inteligente interoperable para la integración de servicios internos y externos
abstract: Hoy en día, gran parte de la información de una organización está repartida en sistemas muy distintos entre sí: repositorios de código, catálogos de datos, bases de datos y muchos otros servicios internos y externos. Esta dispersión dificulta que un agente inteligente pueda acceder a esa información y combinarla de forma unificada. La aparición de los modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño y, sobre todo, del Model Context Protocol (MCP), un estándar abierto y reciente que normaliza la conexión entre modelos de lenguaje y las herramientas y datos que utilizan, abre una vía para resolver este problema. Este Trabajo Fin de Máster, desarrollado en colaboración con CRIDA (Centro de Referencia de Investigación, Desarrollo e Innovación ATM, del inglés Air Traffic Management), tiene como objetivo diseñar e implementar un agente inteligente interoperable, basado en modelos de lenguaje, capaz de obtener información interna y externa a través de servidores MCP. Además, se desarrolla un servidor MCP propio principalmente dirigido a la consulta de datos dentro de la instancia de GitLab. El trabajo empezó con varias pruebas de concepto para familiarizarse con el protocolo y sus distintos mecanismos de transporte. A partir de ahí se implementó un servidor MCP propio para GitLab, que expone 27 herramientas de solo lectura (exploración de repositorios, búsqueda de código, wikis, issues, commits y actividad). En paralelo se integró el servidor MCP oficial de OpenMetadata, centrado en el catálogo de datos y metadatos de CRIDA. Para coordinar ambos dominios sin mezclar contextos, herramientas ni instrucciones, se diseñó una arquitectura formada por un orquestador y varios subagentes especializados, devolviendo los resultados a través de una interfaz web. Por último, se compararon las distintas interfaces de programación que ofrece OpenAI para interactuar con sus modelos, midiendo su latencia y su coste por tokens, y analizando cómo se comporta el almacenamiento en caché de instrucciones (prompt caching). El resultado es un agente interoperable que funciona sobre fuentes reales de la organización. --ABSTRACT-- Nowadays, much of an organization’s information is spread across very different systems: code repositories, data catalogs, databases and many other internal and external services. This makes it hard for an intelligent agent to access that information and combine it in a unified way. The arrival of large language models and, above all, of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a recent open standard that normalizes the connection between language models and the tools and data they use, opens up a way to solve this problem. This Master’s Thesis, carried out in collaboration with CRIDA (Centro de Referencia de Investigación, Desarrollo e Innovación ATM, Air Traffic Management Research, Development and Innovation Reference Centre), aims to design and implement an interoperable intelligent agent, based on language models, able to obtain internal and external information through MCP servers. It also develops a custom MCP server mainly aimed at querying data within the GitLab instance. The work began with several proofs of concept to get familiar with the protocol and its different transport mechanisms. Building on that, a custom MCP server for GitLab was implemented, exposing 27 read-only tools (repository exploration, code search, wikis, issues, commits and activity). In parallel, the official OpenMetadata MCP server was integrated, focused on CRIDA’s data catalog and metadata. To coordinate both domains without mixing contexts, tools or instructions, an architecture made up of an orchestrator and several specialized subagents was designed, returning the results through a web interface. Finally, the different programming interfaces offered by OpenAI to interact with its models were compared by measuring their latency and token cost, and by analyzing how prompt caching behaves. The result is an interoperable agent that works over real organizational sources.
venue: Archivo Digital UPM (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid)
