title: Granum, an agentic-AI GPU discrete element program: verification for dynamic granular flows
abstract: Granum, a GPU discrete element program for soil that an AI agent can drive through theModel Context Protocol, written for quasi-static tests and staged models, was extended fordynamic granular flow with hopper and silo walls, a turning drum, free-falling rigid bodies,grain sinks and counters, initial states read from files and pair-specific contact properties, andwas then tested at three levels. At the contact level it reproduces the impact benchmarksof Chung and Ooi to within 0.1% of Hertz’s solutions. In the DEM8 benchmark of nineopen-source codes it falls inside the codes’ band in all three bulk processes: the four silo flowrates lie within 0.7 to 1.9% of the middle of the band and the ratio of large to small orifice is3.10 against 3.10 ± 0.06, the number of grains in a quadrant of the rotating drum follows thecodes within 246 grains rms with its peaks within 0.04 s and 2%, and the impact paths liewithin the codes’ spread. Against laboratory laws, the discharge of a sand through orifices of5 to 10 grain diameters follows Beverloo’s law with C = 0.54 and k = 1.51, and the collapseof granular columns with aspect ratios of 0.5 to 8 matches the runout of Lube et al. and thefinal height of Lajeunesse et al. once the sand’s shape and rolling resistance are calibratedon its angle of repose. A steel ball penetrates 0.72 to 0.94 times the depth of Uehara etal.’s law, with a stopping time nearly independent of the impact speed as Katsuragi andDurian found, and a 10 t tamper dropped from 5 to 15 m onto a 16 m loose fill reaches adepth of influence of 0.47 to 0.59√WH, within the field range of Mayne et al. The testsalso exposed three defects, a braking effect of fixed drum end plates, a placement step thatignored an impactor’s width, and an all-pairs contact search caused by one large sphere,which are reported with their fixes.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: PyPI API Drift: A Release-Level Record of Public API Changes in 1,872 Popular Python Libraries, with a Checker and a Benchmark for Version-Aware Code Generation
abstract: Abstract Ask a code assistant to append a row to a pandas DataFrame and it may write df.append(row), a method removed in pandas 2.0. Models trained on code from many releases can not tell which API exists in the version a user has installed, and benchmarks of this problem are small and frozen. We present PyPI API Drift, a release-level record of the public APIs of the 1,872 most-downloaded Python libraries: up to 80 recent final releases each (55,565 releases, 2021–October 2026), with signatures, 15,258,652 release-to-release changes and 210,535 deduplicated breaking changes. Extraction is static and import-free, reads only the needed bytes of each wheel, separates names that were truly removed from names that merely left the documented API, and marks with confi dence labels and a coverage layer where static analysis cannot see. It is a high-precision, low-recall record: in AI-agent runtime audits of libraries never used for tuning, 91.9% of high-confidence breaking changes were confirmed, while re call over all runtime-visible changes is limited (16 of 99). On top of it we release an offline checker, lookup tools with an MCP server for coding agents, and VersionProbe, a bench mark of 10,958 valid/invalid snippet pairs. In a preregistered code-repair experiment, repeated across 4 models from one model family, API history from the dataset raised the share of API-compatible, intent-preserving migrations (under our evaluation protocol) to 68.5%–69.9% for every model, from 7.0%–56.6%unaidedand46.2%–62.2%withthenewrelease’s documentation. 13.4% of patch releases contain at least one breaking change.

title: Implementación de un modelo de inteligencia artificial capaz de analizar amenazas en redes corporativas y generar recomendaciones de mitigación personalizadas
abstract: El aumento constante de amenazas cibernéticas generan la necesidad de contar con herra- mientas automatizadas que permiten identificar vulnerabilidades a los administradores de red en la toma de decisiones en base a seguridad. Los métodos tradicionales de análisis suelen requerir altos niveles de especialización y esfuerzo manual considerable, lo que dificulta a su aplicación en entornos de red un poco complejo. El trabajo presente propone el diseño y desarrollo de un sistema web que integra inteligencia artificial para el análisis de vulnerabilidades en redes corporativas. La solución permite realizar escaneo de red y puertos mediante la herramienta Nmap, procesar y estructurar dichos resultados obtenidos. El desarrollo se llevó a cabo utilizando una metodología iterativa compuesta por cinco fases, en las que se implementaron progresivamente la interfaz web, la integración del motor de escaneo, la estructuración de resultados, correlación de vulnerabili- dades y la incorporación de generar recomendaciones de mitigación contextualizadas a través de un modelo de Lenguaje de Gran Escala (LLM). Se hacen el uso de técnicas de procesamiento de lenguaje natural como lo es el Protocolo de Contexto de Modelo (MCP), el sistema transforma la información compleja en descripciones claras y recomendaciones comprensibles, facilitando el entendimiento de los riesgos detectados sin sustituir el criterio del especialista en seguridad. Para evaluar el desempeño del sistema, se realizaron pruebas en varios entornos y se aplicó una encuesta a usuarios que interactuaron con la herramienta. La evaluación se basó en una escala tipo Likert de cinco puntos y consideró aspectos como la usabilidad, la claridad de la interfaz, la confiabilidad de la información obtenida, el desempeño de la inteligencia artificial y la funcionalidad de exportación de resultados en PDF. Los resultados evidencian un alto nivel de satisfacción por los usuarios y una percepción positiva sobre la utilidad del sistema como apoyo al análisis de vulnerabilidades.

title: Perseus MCP - A Bridge between Conversational AI and the Textual Infrastructure of Classical Studies
abstract: Large language models can discuss ancient texts, but they do not automatically possess reliable,current, or passage-level access to the digital libraries on which classical scholarship depends.Perseus MCP addresses this gap by connecting an MCP-capable artificial-intelligence applicationto the Perseus Digital Library and the Scaife Viewer’s search and library services. The projectexposes a set of structured tools for discovering authors and editions, retrieving passages throughCanonical Text Services identifiers, navigating textual references, searching Greek and Latin corpora,and returning evidence in forms that an AI model can process. This paper explains the ModelContext Protocol for readers who are new to the concept, describes the architecture and functionalityof Perseus MCP, and evaluates its usefulness for classical studies, teaching, exploratoryresearch, and reproducible AI-assisted analysis. Particular attention is given to the project’s examplenotebooks, which move from basic endpoint access to complete tool-mediated interactionsinvolving Homer, Philo of Alexandria, and Augustine.

title: AgentNexus: A Boundary-Aware Coordination Architecture for Heterogeneous LLM Code Agents
abstract: Existing multi-agent software development frameworks such as ChatDev and MetaGPT organize agents around roles (product manager, developer, tester) within a single simulated organization. While effective for monolithic tasks, this role-playing paradigm breaks down in real-world polyglot systems where multiple independently-deployed services—each maintained by its own LLM agent—must coordinate across service boundaries. We present AgentNexus, a document exchange center that coordinates heterogeneous code agents at the service granularity rather than the role granularity. AgentNexus introduces three key ideas: (1) a versioned Markdown document store with publish-subscribe notification, enabling agents to detect and respond to cross-service changes; (2) an explicit lifecycle stage model that tracks each service’s development phase as a first-class entity, replacing ad-hoc role-playing with structured state transitions; and (3) a diff-aware update protocol that delivers structured change summaries alongside full document context, allowing downstream agents to perform targeted code modifications. We describe the architecture, implementation, and an initial deployment coordinating a backend search service and its frontend management console. Our results suggest that grounding multi-agent coordination in service-level document exchange—rather than simulated organizational roles—better reflects the structure of real software systems and reduces coordination overhead.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Neural Codec Resonance: Investigating Zero-Shot Generative Music and Speech Forensics via Multi-Resolution Spectral and Phase Invariances
abstract: odels—spanning neural vocoders, latent diffusion architectures,and discrete neural codecs—have enabled the synthesis ofhighly realistic musical pieces and vocal performances. Whiledata-driven classifiers frequently overfit to superficial datasetartifacts, physically grounded methods aim to detect the invariantmathematical footprints imposed by the underlying synthesisarchitectures. In this work, we investigate Neural Codec Resonance(NCR), an analytical framework examining three physical andstructural properties of synthetic audio: (1) ultrasonic codebookbandwidth roll-offs caused by Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ)decimation filters, (2) stereo phase dispersion governed by physicalwave propagation acoustics (the Haas effect) versus pseudo-stereodiffusion collapse, and (3) reconstruction residuals under multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (STFT) autoencoderprojections.Through empirical evaluations across two distinct modalities,we delineate the practical capabilities and boundary conditions ofthese representations: In polyphonic music evaluation (N = 600tracks across five transmission channels: Clean WAV, MP3320 kbps, MP3 128 kbps, AAC 256 kbps, and Opus 16 kbps),stereo phase coherence coupled with ultrasonic boundary trackingachieves robust discrimination between neural music models (Suno,Udio, MusicGen) and acoustic orchestral/jazz studio recordings.Conversely, when evaluating single-channel speech deepfakesin unconstrained real-world settings (N = 60 authentic andsynthetic speech files from open benchmarks), static harmoniccomb heuristics experience substantial degradation (AUROC of0.2844, detection recall of 30.00%, and a false accusation rateof 10.00%), demonstrating that dynamic vocoder pitch tracking,acoustic background noise, and mastered loudness floors confoundsimple spectral peak models. We discuss the implications of thesefindings for automated catalog moderation and voice verificationsystems.Index Terms—Audio Forensics, Generative Music, Neural AudioCodecs, Residual Vector Quantization, Haas Effect, Model ContextProtocol.

title: Startswith, Not Starts-with: A Systematic Study of Path Traversal via Prefix Bypass in the MCP Ecosystem
abstract: Path traversal (CWE-22) is the most critical vulnerability class in file-serving MCP servers, yet the existing defense using str(path).startswith(str(root)) is vulnerable to sibling-directory prefix bypass (CWE-180). We scanned all 1,144 Python MCP servers, found 190 using startswith() for path validation, and confirmed 5 real-world vulnerabilities (file-deletion, file-read, workspace-file operations) across repositories spanning 0-16 stars. All 4 exploitable vulnerabilities were responsibly disclosed. We propose a drop-in fix (Path.relative_to()) and release an automated scanner.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Implementación de dispositivos IoT LoRaWAN en el planeamiento, mantenimiento y control de microrredes que implementan energías renovables
abstract: Este trabajo presenta la arquitectura de gestión integral end-to-end basada en el protocolo LoRaWAN para optimizar microrredes con fuentes de generación renovable en entornos rurales e industriales. La metodología incluyó sensores simplificados y un circuito extensor aislado para conmutar cargas de hasta 400 V y 30 A bajo criterios de seguridad espacial. Asimismo, se integró una capa semántica mediante un servidor de protocolo de contexto de modelo (MCP) acoplado a un modelo de lenguaje de gran escala (LLM) para traducir instrucciones en lenguaje natural a tramas binarias de bajada (downlink). La robustez del ecosistema fue validada empíricamente en tres entornos reales en Colombia. Los resultados de telecomunicaciones demostraron la resiliencia del canal físico ante atenuaciones severas por vegetación, consolidando una Tasa de Error de Paquetes (PER) de tan solo 1.20% bajo modulación SF9. En el análisis eléctrico, la desconexión selectiva automática de cargas aplanó la curva de demanda máxima, reduciendo un 28% el pico de carga (peak shaving). Esta mitigación de reactivos elevó el factor de potencia promedio de 0.74 a 0.88, disminuyendo las pérdidas técnicas óhmicas “ϵ” en un 63.42% y regulando la tensión eficaz dentro de un rango estricto del ±3%. Finalmente, estas optimizaciones disminuyeron el consumo energético general en un 10%, automatizaron el riego con un ahorro de 50 litros de agua diarios y demostraron un periodo de amortización de 10 meses.

title: Pondus: an agentic structural analysis and design program
abstract: Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and itfound fourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the designchecks rather than in the numerical kernels. A second calibration against the verification problems thatCSI publishes for SAP2000 and ETABS reproduced 177 of 199 independent values within 0.5 % andfound eight further defects, including an unconservative omission of the Eurocode 3 moment reductionfor high shear, which led to lumped masses, the SRSS combination and frame shear deformation beingadded. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structural program can be made accurate,whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer must read against the program’s own tables.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Project Thalamus Technical Whitepaper: An Authorship Gate Between Clients and Language Models
abstract: Language models compute answers from scratch on every request, generating new variations even when a prompt has been asked before and human reviewers approved a specific response. This technical whitepaper introduces Project Thalamus, a lightweight proxy that acts as an explicit authorship gate between client applications and language models. Thalamus enforces a deterministic operational rule: Approved Prompts: If an approved answer matches via exact string comparison or MiniLM (or other fine-tuned) cosine similarity (>0.72), Thalamus immediately returns the stored text without invoking the model. Unapproved Prompts: If no approved answer exists, the request routes directly to the model every time without exception. Tool-Bearing Requests: Requests containing function definitions or tools always bypass memory and execute through the model to preserve interactive agent capabilities. Version 0.8 details the verified system architecture utilizing independent local JSON files ("brains") rather than external database services, live-tested system endpoints (including OpenAI-compatible completions and MCP Streamable HTTP transport), comparative benchmarks against RAG and traditional caches, and projected impact at scale. All claims in this document have been verified against running code and an automated test suite.

title: CieveMe/mcp-security-benchmark: v0.1.0 - MCP security benchmark: probe corpus, stdio harness, five scorecards
abstract: MCP security benchmark v0.1. A dependency-free harness that probes MCP servers over stdio and scores them against a fixed corpus of security-relevant cases: read-only contract violations, dangerous tools registered by default, SQL whitelist bypasses, credential exposure, prompt-injection surface, and unredacted output. It exists because "our MCP server is read-only and safe" is a claim, not evidence. The claim becomes evidence when a fixed corpus runs against the server, produces a scorecard, and the harness has been shown to fail a deliberately broken server. Results (2026-09-28, one machine) | target | what it is | verdict | score | tools | findings | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | vulnerable-demo | bundled canary target, insecure on purpose | critical | 4.8 | 6 | 12 | | everything-public | npm @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything | elevated | 88.0 | 13 | 1 | | mysql-ops-mcp-reference | read-only-first MySQL ops server (reference implementation) | no findings | 100.0 | 17 | 0 (+2 advisories) | | filesystem-public | npm @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem | no findings | 100.0 | 14 | 0 | | memory-public | npm @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory | no findings | 100.0 | 9 | 0 | The one high finding: server-everything exposes a get-env tool that returns the process environment; the probe recovered both canary secrets the harness injected. For an agent host, any API key in the server's environment is one tool call away. Reported upstream as modelcontextprotocol/servers#4882. What the score does not mean 100 is not "secure". The corpus has 14 cases; it covers a few well-known failure shapes, not authentication, transport, sandboxing, dependency risk or the target's own business logic. Name-based registration checks are heuristics and are reported as advisories that do not change the score. Detail: results/SUMMARY.md and docs/harness-notes.md. Verify it yourself python -m bench list python -m bench run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Research on the application of AI Agents in design with building information modeling
abstract: Áp dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) trong các dự án xây dựng có tiềm năng rất lớn nhằm tăng năng suất, hiệu quả lao động trong bối cảnh việc triển khai BIM ngày càng mạnh mẽ song hành với sự phát triển bùng nổ của AI thời gian gần đây. Bài báo này tập trung vào việc ứng dụng AI Agent (tác tử AI) như một trợ lý hỗ trợ tự động hóa quá trình thiết kế trên mô hình BIM. Cụ thể, nội dung nghiên cứu trình bày cách thức đơn giản và khả thi để người dùng có thể sử dụng trợ lý AI trong các thao tác nhằm xây dựng hoặc tương tác với mô hình BIM thông qua việc kết nối với phần mềm/công cụ BIM bằng giao thức ngữ cảnh mô hình (MCP). Các ý tưởng, định hướng và yêu cầu của kỹ sư thiết kế có thể đóng gói thành các kỹ năng để hướng dẫn và tích hợp vào trợ lý AI để thực hiện các chuỗi nghiệp vụ một cách hiệu quả. Kết quả của các thử nghiệm ví dụ cho thấy việc áp dụng AI Agent trong BIM ở giai đoạn thiết kế là hoàn toàn khả thi, có tính linh hoạt, khả năng tái sử dụng và giúp tiết kiệm nhiều thời gian và công sức cho các kỹ sư nội nghiệp.

title: VirtualFlyBrain/VFB3-MCP: Release 1.11.1 — repository references point at the org repo
abstract: Per-caller GA4 client IDs and MCP client info tracking Fixes and extends the GA4 usage analytics added in earlier releases: client_id is now derived from a hash of the caller's IP. In stateless HTTP mode there is no session ID, so every caller was previously reported to GA4 under one shared, process-wide id — this made per-user/session analysis in GA4 meaningless. The MCP initialize handshake's clientInfo (which client is connecting — Claude Code, Claude.ai, Codex, etc.) is now captured and sent once per handshake as GA4 user_properties, so it's a real, segmentable dimension GA can report on, persisting onto that caller's later tool-call events. Caller IP is now sent via GA4's ip_override field instead of a custom event param, so GA4 can derive real caller geography for this server-to-server integration (previously every event geo-located to this server's own egress IP). No tool, schema, or request/response behaviour changes — this only affects the optional GA4 analytics integration (GA_MEASUREMENT_ID/GA_API_SECRET). Full changelog: https://github.com/VirtualFlyBrain/VFB3-MCP/compare/v1.11.1...v1.11.2

Uncompressed 16-bit files, the same constraint as volumes. title: I-Lang Protocol Specification
abstract: I-Lang is an AI-native communication protocol that defines a formal vocabulary of 88 verbs, 29 core modifiers plus a 20-key media profile, 25 entities (17 addressable, 8 role), and 13 Greek aliases for structured communication between humans and AI, between AI agents, and within AI internal reasoning. It introduces two syntaxes: operation syntax [] for executable instructions and declaration syntax :: for behavioral identity. Version 3.0 defines the communication format, version 4.0 adds execution semantics, and version 5.0 adds a trainable judgment layer built on an 11-dimensional judgment vector space governed by four axioms and a three-layer architecture, grounded in fuzzy mathematics. I-Lang provides the semantic and judgment layer that sits above tool-integration protocols such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-discovery protocols such as Google's Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A). MIT licensed. Release 5.0-pre.2.1.1 is an erratum on the v5.0 preview line. Section 3 of SPEC-v5.0-PRE.md orders conflicts SURVIVAL > EPISTEMIC, and the reference function f_v5 returns M8 at a STEP-1 survival gate before it reaches the epistemic gate. The section 4 abstain rule required M5 whenever the epistemic gate fires, so a vector that hit both gates had no mode that was both schema-valid and consistent with f_v5. The abstain rule now also accepts M8 on a STEP-1 survival hit. Every other mode under the epistemic gate is still rejected, and M5 stays schema-valid. The reference function, its constants and its weights are unchanged, so no gold label changes. The reference judgment validator ships with the same exception and new self-tests. The grammar validator now reads quoted values as opaque, so a comma, equals sign or bracket inside a quoted value no longer raises E302 or E304, and its canon gate also lints SPEC-v4.1-MEDIA-PROFILE.md. Earlier versions: 5.0-pre.2.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22728994) and 4.1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22729246), both 2026-09-12.

title: Adaptive Model Context Protocols for Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: A new framework for adaptive model context protocols that improve multi-agent cooperation in dispersed environments is presented in this study. The suggested method makes use of dynamic context shar- ing mechanisms that adjust to task complexity, communication band- width, and computational limitations. The framework allows agents to negotiate the best parameters for information exchange by implementing a hierarchical context model with bidirectional context flow. In compar- ison to static approaches, the adaptive protocol lowers communication overhead while preserving task performance, as demonstrated by exper- imental evaluation in distributed sensor networks, autonomous vehicle coordination, and collaborative problem-solving. In order to intelligently filter information exchange, the framework presents context relevance scoring and selective propagation techniques. By providing solutions for autonomous systems functioning under fluctuating resource constraints, this research fills the gap between multi-agent collaboration and dis- tributed systems optimization.
venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management

title: Evaluating Security and Reliability of Stateless Model Context Protocol Gateways
abstract: The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces a stateless request model and routing headers that enable conventional HTTP gateway controls for language-model tools. This study examines whether three deterministic controls—tool-definition pinning, least-privilege tool exposure, and argument-level policy enforcement—prevent unauthorized requests from reaching a backend without rejecting authorized operations. We implemented a minimal HTTP/JSON-RPC gateway prototype and evaluated eight combinations of the controls in a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design. Each configuration received 120 synthetic adversarial requests (40 changed tool descriptors, 40 out-of-scope calls, and 40 disallowed argument sets), 60 valid requests, and 400 timed valid requests over loopback. In this limited implementation, the unprotected baseline rejected none of the 120 adversarial cases, whereas the configuration applying all three controls rejected all 120; each single control rejected precisely the 40 cases constructed to violate its rule. All configurations completed 60 of 60 valid requests. Median observed HTTP latency was 0.533 ms for the baseline and 0.530 ms for the full-control configuration, but these loopback timings do not establish production-scale performance equivalence. The findings demonstrate coverage of the specified access-control invariants, not resistance to model-driven prompt injection. We offer a reproducible pilot methodology and identify the model-in-the-loop, distributed-systems, and identity-validation experiments necessary for stronger external validity.
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Technology Studies

title: Adaptive Model Context Protocols for Trustworthy and Secure Agentic AI Systems
abstract: The Adaptive Model Context Protocols Framework, the proposed AMCP Framework, offers a reliable, safe, and flexible system on which agentic AI can perform based on multi-context settings. The model offers context sensitivity and operational integrity wherein context-aware meta-learning and Bayesian trust estimation, zero-trust security, and federated adversarial defense management are implemented. The performance of the model has been greatly improved as indicated by the results gained after the tests run after 20 training epochs. The accuracy was in the range of 0.71-0.93, the precision was 0.69-0.91 and the recall was 0.66-0.89. The fact that the F1-score consistently converged at 0.90 confirmed dynamic learning, which is balanced understanding of context and policy adaptation and adaptation efficiency of 0.78 to 0.92. In general, they show that the AMCP framework can ensure that the AI responds in a safe and sensitive way depending on its surroundings. It is also able to support clear-cut decision making which is rather essential to autonomous and ethical stable AI systems.
venue: International Journal of Computer Technology and Electronics Communication

title: SUMO-MCP: Leveraging the Model Context Protocol for Autonomous Traffic Simulation and Optimization
abstract: Traffic simulation tools, such as SUMO, are essential for urban mobility research. However, such tools remain challenging for users due to complex manual workflows involving network download, demand generation, simulation setup, and result analysis. In this paper, we introduce SUMO-MCP, a novel platform that not only wraps SUMO' s core utilities into a unified tool suite but also provides additional auxiliary utilities for common preprocessing and postprocessing tasks. Using SUMO-MCP, users can issue simple natural-language prompts to generate traffic scenarios from OpenStreetMap data, create demand from origin-destination matrices or random patterns, run batch simulations with multiple signal-control strategies, perform comparative analyses with automated reporting, and detect congestion for signal-timing optimization. Furthermore, the platform allows flexible custom workflows by dynamically combining exposed SUMO tools without additional coding. Experiments demonstrate that SUMO-MCP significantly makes traffic simulation more accessible and reliable for researchers. We will release code for SUMO-MCP at https://github.com/ycycycl/SUMO-MCP in the future.

title: Building a Simple Internet Search App Using Anthropic Model Context Protocol
abstract: Introduction The Anthropic Model Context Protocol (AMCP) is an open standard protocol that enables developers to provide context to LLMs. It represents a significant advancement in how we interact with AI assistants. By connecting Claude with external tools and services, AMCP enhances Claude's capabilities beyond its built-in knowledge.

title: Formula 1 Model Context Protocol Platform for LLMs Using Cloud Computing
abstract: This study presents a Formula 1 Model Context Protocol (MCP) platform for systematically evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) equipped with identical tools and datasets. The research addresses standardisation challenges in Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool integration by leveraging Anthropic's MCP to enable LLM-agnostic interactions with Formula 1 telemetry data. The implementation provides access to extensive F1 datasets including lap times, telemetry, weather conditions, tire strategies, and race results through 15 specialised tools, supporting three major LLM providers. Experimental evaluation examines model performance across three query categories: simple data retrieval, complex analytical reasoning requiring tool chaining, and ambiguous queries testing contextual understanding. Results reveal significant behavioural differences despite standardised tool access. While all models demonstrated consistent tool selection accuracy, substantial variations emerged in response richness and analytical depth. Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) and Claude models provided comprehensive, analytically rich responses with contextual insights, whereas Gemini models exhibited limited elaboration despite achieving correct answers. The most notable finding concerns varying impacts of training knowledge cutoffs on tool utilisation. Claude 3.7 Sonnet exhibited complete tool activation failure when queried about 2025 data, explicitly refusing to search beyond its knowledge boundary. On the other hand, GPT models successfully accessed tools for identical queries but exhibited hallucinations, referencing non-existent drivers. This highlights a fundamental trade-off between conservative accuracy and dynamic information retrieval. The research contributes empirical evidence of model-specific behaviours within standardised MCP environments, demonstrating that while MCP effectively standardises tool integration, underlying LLM selection significantly impacts application performance, particularly in contextual understanding, creative elaboration, and temporal knowledge boundary handling.

title: MIDAS: A Library of Integration Defects in Model Context Protocol (MCP)-Based Systems
abstract: MIDAS is a curated library of integration defects in software systems that use the Model Content Protocol (MCP. This v1 release contains 159 confirmed defects across 33 open source MCP-based systems, collected by mining GitHub issue trackers and manually classified into recurring defect patterns. The release contains the defect records, studied system metadata, and the collection scripts. Accompanies our empirical study of MCP integration defects.

title: CryptoMCP: Model Context Protocol Server for Real-Time On-Chain & Market Telemetry
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server providing real-time cryptographic asset intelligence, live orderbook telemetry, and transaction validation interfaces for autonomous LLM agents.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Model Context Protocol: The Central Nervous System for a New Generation of Artificially Intelligent Agents
abstract: As multi-agent AI systems evolve from prototypes to production-grade enterprise applications, the need for a robust and scalable communication architecture has become an operational imperative. However, traditional approaches like linear chaining or ad-hoc peer-to-peer messaging result in brittle, unmanageable systems that lack observability and fail to handle the non-deterministic nature of AI agents. To address this architectural deficiencies, this paper introduces the Message, Context, and Protocol (MCP) framework, an architectural pattern designed to serve as a communication backbone and "central nervous system" for complex AI systems by decoupling agent intent from execution. Performance evaluations under simulated enterprise load demonstrate that by decoupling agents through a central message bus and a stateful orchestrator, MCP maintains system resilience and prevents catastrophic failure even under high load (500 req/sec), although the orchestrator itself is identified as a primary bottleneck requiring horizontal scaling. These results underscore that centralized state management is not merely an option but a necessity for enterprise AI, providing the modularity and fault tolerance required to transition agentic workflows from experimental concepts to reliable business solutions.

title: Model Context Protocol Driven Reinforcement Learning Framework for Next Generation LLM Training
abstract: Most Large Language Models (LLMs) perform particularly well on tasks, but often they are highly unstable, fail to follow their policies, and are unpredictable when using adversarial, ambiguous, or risky prompts. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a Protocol-Driven Reinforcement Learning (PD-RL) framework which incorporates protocol reasoning into the learning and optimization pipeline. The design is based on validator-nonrewarded reward signals, multi-step execution of the reinforcement process, the prioritized replay of non-compliant outputs, and an autonomous repair process to ensure behavior adhering to rules is stable without a reduction in utility. It uses a common evaluation environment to compare PD-RL with two baseline models in terms of several dimensions, such as compliance, governance drift, utility, rare-case reliability, computation overhead, and recovery speed. The findings reveal that PD-RL allows obtaining over 90 percent compliance, greatly reducing governance violations, and quickly recovering safe behavior within minutes. These results prove that the combination of protocol constraints with reinforcement learning produces not only the performant but effectively aligned and reliable LLMs. Therefore, PD-RL provides a capable and scalable channel to build reliable LLMs that can be applied in enterprises and safety issues.
venue: International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)

title: Model Context Protocol Servers for Intelligent Optimization: From Primitive Operations to Complex Problem Solving
abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has reshaped AI applications, yet connecting them with specialized computational platforms continues to be a complex task. Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers provide a unified interface that enables LLMs to interact with external systems through basic operations. In this paper, we demonstrate how MCP servers can transform arbitrary computational platforms into intelligent problem-solving environments by exposing low-level primitives that LLMs can assemble into sophisticated optimization procedures. We introduce a new paradigm that (i) frames optimization problems as intelligent control tasks and (ii) allows LLMs to discover solutions without relying on explicitly coded algorithms. Through both a matrix-based toy example and a practical Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) case study, we show how simple primitives (for example, pixel modifications or node state queries) can be orchestrated by LLMs to solve complex optimization challenges, including constraint satisfaction and boundary detection. Our analysis shows that this approach offers performances similar to those of existing well-known algorithms, while offering more flexibility and intuitive programmability based on natural language. We present MCP servers as a core framework for enhancing access to optimization problem-solving via natural language interfaces.
venue: International Conference on Future Networks and Distributed Systems (ICFNDS)

title: From Artificial Intelligence Ready to Artificial Intelligence Accessible: Public Health Agencies Need Model Context Protocols.
Graphiti Model Context Protocol Server: Implementation and Performance Evaluation of a Knowledge-graph-based AI Code Intelligence Framework
abstract: In this study, we introduce the Graphiti Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, an AIassisted programming framework that integrates a time-aware knowledge graph with the MCP to enhance contextual sensing and semantic reasoning in intelligent code generation.The system addresses key limitations of existing AI agents in long-term software engineering tasksparticularly the lack of persistent memory and insufficient contextual perception.The proposed architecture consists of an MCP client, the Graphiti MCP core server, a Neo4j-based knowledge graph database, and semantic sensing modules connected to the OpenAI Application Programming Interface.Together, these components enable dynamic knowledge retrieval, crossfile context fusion, and adaptive code assistance.Experiments conducted on 1000 open-source software projects demonstrate statistically significant improvements: code completion accuracy (CCA@1) increased from 45.3 to 68.5%, contextual relevance score improved from 3.0 to 4.2, and task completion time decreased by approximately 35.5%.Furthermore, a mathematical model is developed to describe how graph-based knowledge retrieval enhances effective memory sensing and contextual stability, providing a theoretical foundation for intelligent programming.The results verify that the Graphiti MCP Server offers substantial potential for advancing context-aware and sensor-like AI systems with semantic sensing and adaptive contextual reasoning capabilities in software development environments.However, current AIassisted programming systems still suffer from several limitations, including restricted longterm memory, fragmented contextual understanding, and insufficient semantic perception in large-scale software development environments.To address these challenges, we propose a knowledge-graph-based context-aware semantic sensing and contextual reasoning framework that integrates semantic retrieval, persistent memory, and adaptive context fusion through the Graphiti MCP Server architecture.Although the proposed framework significantly improves

title: Task-Oriented Communications for Agentic IoT: An LLM-Driven QoS/Security Policy Generation via Dynamic Model Context Protocol
abstract: The emergence of Agentic IoT, where autonomous intelligent agents such as mobile robots, UAVs, and industrial actuators independently execute complex missions, demands communication and security configurations that can adapt to both fast mission-driven changes and slower environment-driven performance drifts. Existing control paradigms are inadequate. Specifically, static policies cannot react to real-time variations, while task-aware adaptive policies largely overlook environmental dynamics, leaving systems vulnerable to network degradation and latency spikes. To address these limitations, we propose the Dynamic Model Context Protocol (dMCP), a cognitive control framework that bridges high-level mission intents with lowlevel system configurations via the standardized MCP interface. dMCP employs a Large Language Model to reason over real-time mission and environment contexts, generating executable policy vectors. An event-driven trigger mechanism re-evaluates policies upon abrupt mission changes or significant environmental drifts, ensuring timely adaptation without overreacting to transient fluctuations. Simulation results demonstrate that dMCP achieves higher reliability, reduced tail latency, and improved Service Level Objective compliance compared with both static and taskaware adaptive baselines, making it a viable control paradigm for highly dynamic Agentic IoT deployments.
venue: International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)

title: Kali Linux Meets AI: From ATT&CK-Aligned Tooling to Model Context Protocol and Natural-Language Penetration Testing
abstract: The discipline of offensive security has matured considerably over the past decade, transitioning from ad hoc tool usage toward structured, framework-aligned methodologies that mirror the behavior of real-world threat actors. Kali Linux 2025.2 represents the state of the art in penetration testing platform design, providing over 600 tools organized into functional categories that map to the MITRE ATT&CK framework’s tactical phases. This chapter examines the architecture and practical application of Kali Linux MCP integration, documenting how IT security professionals can configure Claude Desktop and other LLM clients to execute Nmap, Metasploit, Nikto, Gobuster, Hydra, and other Kali tools through natural-language prompting. Detailed installation procedures based on the sdntechforum/kali-mcp reference implementation and the official mcp-kali-server Kali package are provided, followed by realistic operational scenarios demonstrating AI-orchestrated reconnaissance, exploitation chain development, and post-assessment reporting. The chapter closes by examining the offensive-context security risks unique to MCP – prompt injection from target-controlled content, over-delegation to AI judgment, data exposure to cloud-hosted LLM providers, and the sandbox-isolation discipline that makes the Kali host itself the failure-containment boundary for AI-orchestrated offensive workflows – and bridges into Chapter 9 ’s treatment of full adversary-emulation campaigns through MITRE Caldera.

title: AgentK: detecção inteligente de erros em arquivos de configuração do Kubernetes, uma implementação do Model Context Protocol
abstract: O crescimento do uso de contêineres e sua orquestração com Kubernetes tem trazido benefícios de escalabilidade e padronização, mas também desafios relacionados a falhas de configuração, responsáveis por grande parte dos incidentes de segurança na plataforma. Nesse cenário, este trabalho apresenta o AgentK, um sistema baseado em Large Language Models (LLM) e no Model Context Protocol (MCP), desenvolvido para a detecção inteligente de erros em arquivos YAML (Ain't Markup Language) do Kubernetes. A pesquisa foi conduzida em ambiente controlado com Minikube e infraestrutura do provedor de nuvem Amazon Web Service (AWS), utilizando arquivos com falhas intencionais. Foram comparados diferentes modelos quanto a custo, tempo de resposta e capacidade de detecção. Os resultados mostraram que o o4-mini obteve 100% de acurácia, mas apresentou limitações de integração; já o gpt-4.1, embora tenha identificado 66,7% das falhas, foi escolhido por oferecer melhor equilíbrio entre custo, que representa cerca de 28,5% menor que o o4-mini , desempenho e compatibilidade arquitetural. A arquitetura final permitiu não apenas detectar, mas também corrigir falhas automaticamente, evidenciando o potencial do AgentK para reforçar a segurança e a robustez de ambientes Kubernetes, especialmente em cenários críticos como cidades inteligentes.
venue: FTT Journal of Engineering and Business

title: RULES AS DATA: A GOVERNED, DUAL-TRANSPORT MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL SERVER FOR SAFE LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL ACCESS TO ENTERPRISE ERP DATA

abstract: This book will inform readers on constructing .NET applications with AI features using Model Context Protocol.

title: Agentic Modelling Pipeline: Reproducible Rapid Stormwater Modelling Management System with OpenClaw
abstract: Configuring urban hydrological models, such as SWMM, for operational or real-time modelling remains onerous for many models. We propose an Agentic SWMM workflow, which embeds ‘Skills’ and model context protocols to automate model configuration, execution, and extract and plot quantities of interest. To ensure that the entire Agentic SWMM workflow is auditable and reproducible, each run will create an independent manifest file that documents the SWMM version used, parameter mappings, input file hashes, and quality gate (e.g., continuity diagnostics). We demonstrate the workflow on the Tod Creek watershed (located on the Saanich Peninsula, British Columbia) and verified the equivalence between EPA SWMM® command line execution and model context protocol triggered SWMM execution, and between SWMM GUI workflow and the Agentic SWMM workflow. Validation was demonstrated through identical peak. The overall automation workflow (Skills and model context protocol setting), along with plotting services and evaluation protocols are available as Open Source to support a reproducible Agentic SWMM workflow triggered by natural language.

title: HiroYokoyama/moleditpy-mcp_server: MoleditPy MCP Server 1.5.0
abstract: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server plugin for MoleditPy that exposes the molecular editor to AI assistants. Enables molecule loading, editing, 3D visualization, DFT input file generation, and plugin authoring via natural-language conversation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: UralicMCP: Turning LLMs into Experts in Endangered Languages with MCP
abstract: This paper introduces a new MCP (Model Context Protocol) feature to UralicNLP Python library, UralicMCP. The MCP server exposes rule-based tools such as morphological analyzer, inflector, lemmatizer and dictionaries to any LLM tool that supports MCP. With the help of these tools, LLMs have a shot in completing NLP tasks in languages they know virtually nothing about.

title: Machina: An AI Agent Framework for Industrial Maintenance
abstract: Machina is an open-source Python framework for building AI agents specialized in industrial maintenance (predictive, preventive, corrective). It provides pre-built connectors for industrial systems (CMMS, IoT sensors, ERP), a domain model aligned with ISO 14224, and an LLM-powered agent layer with domain-aware prompting.

title: CASPER Astro Tools: open astronomy tools for AI agents and scripts
abstract: A standalone, read-only toolkit of 46 astronomy tools (literature, public archives, offline calculators) exposed as a Python API, a command line and a Model Context Protocol server, with a generated tool catalogue and a seed benchmark (CASPER AstroToolBench) for tool-using language models. It is the open, public part of CASPER, the assistant platform of CAMCEAD at the Institute of Astronomy, University of Cambridge.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: After the Agent
abstract: After the Agent is an experimental browser instrument for repairing inherited configuration and queued work in a simulated light installation. A deterministic engine supports browser interaction, a local Model Context Protocol server and a headless runner. An independent Python oracle checks repairs against twelve fixed future scenarios. The source includes a retained model setup demonstration, separately labelled authored fixtures and reproducible software checks. Human usability, recovery benefit, learning effects and transfer to production systems have not been established. Research collection is disabled.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP + SKILL: A Deterministic Architecture for Enterprise AI Automation with Selective Intelligence Application
Introduction to Practical Tools
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in product development is transitioning from basic code generation to comprehensive, agent-driven workflow automation. Google Antigravity leads this shift through an agent-first architecture that enables a Product Manager (PM) to move beyond writing standard requirement documents to orchestrating tangible outcomes. This chapter explores the avenues that enable leveraging integrated chat interfaces, centralized agent management, and Model Context Protocol endpoints that professionals can securely connect external tools and manage autonomous agents that plan, execute, and verify complex tasks across multiple systems.

title: Modeling Human Responses to Multimodal AI Content
abstract: As AI-generated content becomes widespread, so does the risk of misinformation. While prior research has primarily focused on identifying whether content is authentic, much less is known about how such content influences human perception and behavior. In domains like trading or the stock market, predicting how people react (e.g., whether a news post will go viral), can be more critical than verifying its factual accuracy. To address this, we take a human-centered approach and introduce the MhAIM Dataset, which contains 154,552 online posts (111,153 of them AI-generated), enabling large-scale analysis of how people respond to AI-generated content. Our human study reveals that people are better at identifying AI content when posts include both text and visuals, particularly when inconsistencies exist between the two. We propose three new metrics: trustworthiness, impact, and openness, to quantify how users judge and engage with online content. We present T-Lens, an LLM-based agent system designed to answer user queries by incorporating predicted human responses to multimodal information. At its core is HR-MCP (Human Response Model Context Protocol), built on the standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling seamless integration with any LLM. This integration allows T-Lens to better align with human reactions, enhancing both interpretability and interaction capabilities. Our work provides empirical insights and practical tools to equip LLMs with human-awareness capabilities. By highlighting the complex interplay among AI, human cognition, and information reception, our findings suggest actionable strategies for mitigating the risks of AI-driven misinformation.

title: Evolving iPaaS to Autonomous Integration with Generative AI
abstract: This paper discusses a holistic approach to evolve traditional enterprise system integration, leveraging Large Language Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation and the Model Context Protocol to build ‘Autonomous Integration with AI Agents’. I have proposed a roadmap to a paradigm shift from traditional, static integration flows built with integration platform offerings to a dynamic, context-aware integration ecosystem. By enabling AI agents to autonomously negotiate contracts and protocols and by using MCP to standardize contextual data exchange, the aim is to address the challenges of complexity, adaptability, and interoperability in modern enterprise systems, ultimately trending towards reduced development time, adaptable to modern agile practices, and enhanced system resilience.
venue: International Journal of Computer Trends and Technology

title: ESHM20-MCP: an LLM-agent interface to the 2020 European Seismic Hazard and Risk Models
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing the 2020 European Seismic Hazard Model (ESHM20) and the 2020 European Seismic Risk Model (ESRM20) through 24 typed endpoints, backed by OpenQuake hazardlib. Covers hazard curves, uniform hazard and conditional mean spectra, surface (site-amplified) hazard, damage and average annual loss, retrofit comparison, per-tectonic-region custom ground-motion model substitution, and conditional-spectrum record selection from the Engineering Strong-Motion database. Companion code to Vemula, Jehel, Cotton and Gatti, "An LLM-Agent Interface for End-to-End Probabilistic Seismic Hazard and Risk Analysis" (npj Natural Hazards, in review).
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: vcfclick: embedded VCF databases with auditable natural-language queries
abstract: Small VCF databases, one per cohort. Variants, genotypes, and samples live in either chDB (embedded ClickHouse) or DuckDB; gene and ClinVar annotations live in a sibling DuckDB file. A bundled Model Context Protocol server exposes a small set of tools so a language-model client can query the cohort in natural language and see the SQL it generated. Designed for the gap between bcftools/cyvcf2 (single-file, no persistence) and Hail/TileDB-VCF (cluster-scale). Atomic two-phase ingest with rollback, sparse-aware cohort allele-frequency math, parallel ingest with index-aware region splitting, and Arrow/Parquet as a public interchange format via db dump and db ingest-parquet.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: MCP + SKILL: A Deterministic Architecture for Enterprise AI Automation with Selective Intelligence Application
abstract: This paper introduces MCP + SKILL (Model Context Protocol + Structured Knowledge and Instruction Layer for LLM), a framework for enterprise AI automation achieving deterministic workflow execution with selective intelligence application. Key Results:- 97.9% reduction in LLM API costs- 85.3% improvement in execution latency - 100% output determinism for identical inputs The architecture uses four layers: orchestration, SKILL workflow files, MCP tool servers, and external integrations. The key innovation is formalizing decision points where LLM reasoning provides genuine value, with conditional routing that invokes AI only at these points. Methodology: Design Science Research with B2B customer onboarding case study. Code: https://github.com/debray2523/mcp-skill-automation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Catalunya 2022 - RESET: Crida per reactivar el país

title: Sensor Data Reliability Assessment for Safe LLM Control of Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into control loops of Cyber-Physical Systems introduces significant reliability and safety challenges related to input data quality. When decisions are based on unreliable or incomplete sensor data, even correct LLM reasoning can lead to dangerous actions. We propose a Trust-Gated Model Context Protocol (MCP), a safety middleware that evaluates sensor-data reliability before allowing the LLM to execute actions. Multiple anomaly detection mechanisms compute a dynamic trust score reflecting data quality, enabling full autonomy under reliable conditions and preemptive action restriction when anomalies are detected. Experimental evaluation on a simulated microalgal bioreactor with eight fault scenarios demonstrates zero unsafe execution rate.
venue: Pan-Hellenic Conference on Progress in Computing and Informatics (PCI)

title: Defensive Publications — Technology Outlaws LLC — AI Inference Security Architecture Prior Art (DP-001 through DP-005)
abstract: Five technical disclosures establishing prior art for the Technology Outlaws LLC patent portfolio. Covers: (DP-001) compliance wire protocol frame schema with SimHash content fingerprinting and derivative-only persistence; (DP-002) attacker-perspective large language model pipeline gate for CI/CD security with VNet-constrained model invocation and supply chain integrity verification; (DP-003) multi-layer pre-authentication OSI gate architecture for structural elimination of pre-auth RCE attack surface; (DP-004) database-backed Model Context Protocol server with compound query tier; (DP-005) quantum random number generator seeded moving target defense for AI inference infrastructure. All disclosures are covered by provisional patent applications filed with the USPTO prior to publication.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: AI Assistant for Rapid Modelling and Design of Aircraft
abstract: Collaborative aircraft design environments face significant challenges in intuitive geometry manipulation and tool integration. This research develops an AI-assisted interface using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to bridge natural language commands with established aerospace tools. The approach integrates large language models with three specialized applications for optimization, visualization, and aircraft geometry modification. Results demonstrate successful implementation, enabling designers to accomplish complex tasks such as multi-objective optimization and empennage reconfiguration through conversational prompts. While occasional AI misinterpretations required prompt refinement, the system proved effective at translating intent into precise tool operations. The study concludes that MCP provides a viable framework for creating intuitive design interfaces while maintaining accuracy via integration with domain-specific computational methods.
venue: EASN International Conference on Innovation in Aviation & Space Towards Sustainability Today & Tomorrow

title: The Open Source Economic Index of AI Adoption and Capability
abstract: We work towards measuring both AI adoption and the capability of AI to perform discrete labor tasks across various occupations. To measure adoption, we develop an open-source economic index that uses publicly available user-LLM chat data and O*NET tasks to replicate studies produced by frontier AI labs, finding that occupations in the finance, computer science, and arts sectors are those with the highest adoption rates. To measure capabilities, we build a system that generates benchmark scenarios grounded in O*NET occupations, tasks, and model-context-protocol (MCP) servers. We test Kimi-k2.5 with an OpenAI agents SDK harness on scenarios across 9 occupations that appear frequently in our index, finding that AI correctly executes high-level workflows but often errs in the granular details (such as specific tool calls used).

title: THE EVOLUTION OF THE SEMANTIC WEB: FROM FOUNDATIONAL TRIPLES TO THE AGENTIC ERA
abstract: This paper analyzes the evolution of the Semantic Web into the ""Agentic Web"", a digital ecosystem designed for autonomous AI agents. This transformation is driven by advanced W3C standards like RDF 1.2, which introduces triple terms to streamline complex metadata management and optimize graph storage. A critical focus of the research is the neuro-symbolic integration of these structured knowledge graphs with Large Language Models (LLMs) to mitigate AI hallucinations and enable accurate reasoning. Additionally, the paper explores how the emerging Web Model Context Protocol allows traditional websites to expose structured, agent-ready tools natively in the browser. Finally, it examines the necessity of Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials, which provide a cryptographic trust layer enabling AI agents to securely authenticate, negotiate, and transact across different domains without requiring constant human oversight.

title: DBot: AI-Driven Multi-Database Monitoring and Diagnostics Platform
abstract: DBot is an AI-driven monitoring and diagnostics platform designed to provide a unified view of heterogeneous database systems including MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis. The platform integrates a FastAPI-based orchestration backend, Model Context Protocol (MCP) agents for database-specific telemetry collection and checks, and a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning layer implemented using PydanticAI. DBot also provides a React-based dashboard that combines real-time metrics visualization with a conversational interface for natural language queries. This report documents the design, implementation, and evaluation of DBot, and demonstrates how modular agents and LLM-assisted reasoning can reduce manual effort in diagnosis while improving observability across multiple database technologies. Keywords: AIOps, database monitoring, MCP agents, FastAPI, Pydantic AI, LLM, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, observability.

title: unimodpy: A Python library for the UNIMOD mass spectrometry modifications database
abstract: unimodpy is a typed Python package for parsing and querying the UNIMOD protein modification database used in mass spectrometry-based proteomics. It ships with a bundled UNIMOD OBO file so it works offline, parses OBO source files into typed, frozen dataclasses (UnimodEntry, Specificity, NeutralLoss), and exposes a queryable UnimodDatabase with lookup by integer ID, UNIMOD accession string, case-insensitive name, and full-text search. It computes elemental composition and Hill-notation ProForma formulas, including monosaccharide abbreviation expansion and isotope label support, and offers TSV/CSV export and a round-trip OBO writer. An optional FastAPI and Model Context Protocol server exposes the same database over HTTP. unimodpy is intended for proteomics software, annotation pipelines, and research scripts that need programmatic access to UNIMOD modification data. It requires Python 3.12 or later.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Automated Power Dispatch Architecture Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Traditional power dispatch struggles to adapt to the uncertainty of renewable energy. Here we propose a Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaborative Architecture for Power Dispatch (DMAC-PD). The architecture includes dynamically reasoning and invoking tools through the Main Agent while integrating domain knowledge by the Knowledge Agent, ensuring physical and power stability constraints through the Safety Agent, and integrating various power system computation tools. The architecture employs a power dispatch model context protocol to coordinate the invocation of heterogeneous power system computation tools, supporting end-to-end automated processes from task analysis to strategy generation. Case studies show that the system can comprehensively integrate the uncertainties of wind-solar power prediction and load fluctuations, generate power system scheduling plans that comply with physical constraints, and provide an automated solution for intelligent dispatch in power grids.
